6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0ChartPair
7	
8	/-!
9	# C9b: what `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` of a chart map actually asks for
10	
11	`Picard/Pic0ChartPair.lean` pins `IsChartUniv` — the `hf` half of the `(f, hf)` pair that
12	`pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` consumes — and its docstring, together with the `c9b` roadmap
13	row, prices it as **one** obligation: the relative form of DAT-C GAP-2 plus the classifier,
14	CERT-Σ-gated.
15	
16	**That pricing is wrong, and this file is the correction.**  `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` is
17	`MorphismProperty.relative` at `yoneda` (mathlib `MorphismProperty/Representable.lean`), and
18	`relative` is *by definition* a conjunction of two independent statements:
19	
20	1. **relative representability** — for every test `T` and every `g : yoneda.obj T ⟶ 𝓟`, the
21	   fibre product of the chart map along `g` is representable *by a scheme*;
22	2. **the property clause** — every represented pullback is an open immersion of schemes.
23	
24	The GAP-2/classifier story is the input to (2) only: it is what makes the fibre a single
25	point, hence the represented pullback an open subscheme.  It says nothing about (1), which
26	is a representability statement about a fibre product.  Read as one clause, a lane waits on
27	CERT-Σ for both halves.  Read as two, half of the work is stateable and provable *now*, with
28	no divisor-representability endpoint and no certificate anywhere in it.
29	
30	## What this file provides, and what it deliberately does not
31	
32	Everything here is stated for an **arbitrary** morphism of big-site presheaves
33	`f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1` and an **arbitrary** open `V ⊆ X`.  No `divRep`
34	endpoint, no certificate, no `Z`, no `θ` and no chart index appears in any statement.  That
35	is the point: `IsChartUniv` becomes *this criterion instantiated at* `abelSigmaChart`, and
36	the divisor-representability shape enters only at the instantiation.
37	
38	The criterion's hypotheses are **elementwise** conditions on the presheaf — a fibrewise
39	injectivity clause and a clause producing the representing open — because that is what
40	mathlib's `MorphismProperty.relative.of_exists` reduces the goal to once the presheaf
41	category's pullbacks are computed pointwise (`Types.isPullback_iff`).
42	
43	## Main declarations
44	
45	* `AlgebraicGeometry.ChartFibrePresented` — the elementwise datum (1) needs: for each test
46	  point `g` of the target, an open `W` of the test and an identification of the `W`-points
47	  with the chart points hitting `g`.  This is the *shape* of a fibre-product presentation,
48	  named so that a producer knows exactly what it owes.
49	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isOpenImmersion_presheaf_of_chartFibrePresented` — **the criterion**:
50	  a `ChartFibrePresented` datum gives `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf f`, discharging BOTH clauses
51	  at once.  Certificate-free and divRep-free.
52	* `AlgebraicGeometry.mono_of_isOpenImmersion_presheaf` — the converse direction that makes
53	  the split honest: `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf f` *implies* `f` is a monomorphism.  So "the
54	  Abel map is not a monomorphism", which three files cite as the reason the unrestricted
55	  certificate fails, is a consequence of the criterion rather than an extra obligation — and
56	  it shows the elementwise injectivity clause below is **necessary**, not an artefact of
57	  this route.
58	* `AlgebraicGeometry.injective_of_isOpenImmersion_presheaf` — the same fact in the
59	  elementwise form a chart-locus argument can actually use.
60	-/
61	
62	set_option autoImplicit false
63	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
64	
65	universe u
66	
67	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
68	
69	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
70	
71	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
72	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
73	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
74	
75	noncomputable section
76	
77	/-! ## The necessary direction: an open immersion of presheaves is a monomorphism
78	
79	Stated first, because it is what tells us the criterion below asks for the right thing. -/
80	
81	/-- **An open immersion of presheaves out of a representable is a monomorphism.**
82	
83	This is mathlib's `presheaf_mono_of_le` at `P := IsOpenImmersion`, whose hypothesis
84	`IsOpenImmersion ≤ monomorphisms Scheme` is the landed `IsOpenImmersion.le_monomorphisms`.
85	
86	Recorded because the whole chart layer rests on the sentence "the Abel map is not a
87	monomorphism, so `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` is false for the unrestricted divisor scheme"
88	(`Pic0AtlasFromDivRep.lean:54`, repeated in `Pic0ChartPair.lean:14`).  That sentence is a
89	*derivation*, not an independent input, and this lemma is the derivation. -/
90	theorem mono_of_isOpenImmersion_presheaf {X : Scheme.{u}}
91	    {f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1} (hf : IsOpenImmersion.presheaf f) :
92	    Mono f :=
93	  MorphismProperty.presheaf_mono_of_le IsOpenImmersion.le_monomorphisms hf
94	
95	/-- **The elementwise form of the necessary direction**: if `f` is an open immersion of
96	presheaves then on every test it is injective on points.
97	
98	This is the clause `ChartFibrePresented.fibre_injective` below, read backwards, and it is
99	why that clause is not an artefact of this particular route: any proof of
100	`IsOpenImmersion.presheaf f` whatsoever yields it.  For the Abel chart it is exactly "the
101	normalized effective representative is unique", i.e. the relative form of DAT-C GAP-2 — so
102	GAP-2 is *forced* by the target, not merely sufficient for it. -/
103	theorem injective_of_isOpenImmersion_presheaf {X : Scheme.{u}}
104	    {f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1} (hf : IsOpenImmersion.presheaf f)
105	    (T : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ) :
106	    Function.Injective (f.app T) :=
107	  (mono_iff_injective (f.app T)).mp
108	    ((NatTrans.mono_iff_mono_app f).mp (mono_of_isOpenImmersion_presheaf hf) T)
109	
110	/-! ## The sufficient direction: the elementwise datum, and the criterion -/
111	
112	variable (C) in
113	/-- **The fibre of a chart map over one test point, presented by an open of the test.**
114	
115	This is the datum mathlib's `relative.of_exists` asks for at a single
116	`g : yoneda.obj T ⟶ pic0SigmaSheaf C`, written out so a producer can see exactly what it
117	owes.  Given a chart map `f` out of `X`:
118	
119	* `W` is an open subscheme of the test `T` — the locus where the class named by `g` *is* a
120	  chart value.  For the Abel chart this is `chartLocus`;
121	* `r` recovers the chart point: over `W`, the divisor family whose class `g` is;
122	* `sq` says the two ways round agree;
123	* `exists_factor` is the honest content — a test point of `X` and a test point of `T` with
124	  the *same* class come from a unique point of `W`.  Existence is coverage-on-the-locus;
125	  the uniqueness half is *not* a field here, because it is free: `W.ι` is a monomorphism.
126	
127	Nothing in this structure mentions a divisor scheme, a certificate, a twist or a chart
128	index.  It is a statement about a morphism of presheaves and an open of a test. -/
129	structure ChartFibrePresented {X T : Scheme.{u}}
130	    (f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1) (g : yoneda.obj T ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
131	    where
132	  /-- The locus of the test where the class named by `g` is a chart value. -/
133	  W : T.Opens
134	  /-- The chart point over that locus. -/
135	  r : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ X
136	  /-- The square commutes: `r` names the class `g` restricted to `W`. -/
137	  sq : yoneda.map r ≫ f = yoneda.map W.ι ≫ g
138	  /-- **Coverage on the locus**: an `S`-point of `X` and an `S`-point of `T` carrying the
139	  same class factor through `W`, compatibly with both projections. -/
140	  exists_factor : ∀ (S : Scheme.{u}) (v : S ⟶ X) (w : S ⟶ T),
141	    f.app (op S) v = g.app (op S) w → ∃ u : S ⟶ (W : Scheme.{u}), u ≫ r = v ∧ u ≫ W.ι = w
142	
143	namespace ChartFibrePresented
144	
145	variable {X T : Scheme.{u}} {f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1}
146	  {g : yoneda.obj T ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1}
147	
148	/-- **The datum presents the fibre product**: the square of `ChartFibrePresented` is a
149	pullback of presheaves.
150	
151	Pullbacks in a presheaf category are computed pointwise
152	(`IsPullback.of_forall_isPullback_app`), and a pointwise pullback of types is exactly
153	"commutes + jointly injective + jointly surjective" (`Types.isPullback_iff`).  The first is
154	`sq`, the third is `exists_factor`, and the second is free from `W.ι` being a
155	monomorphism — which is where the openness of `W` does its work. -/
156	theorem isPullback (D : ChartFibrePresented C f g) :
157	    IsPullback (yoneda.map D.r) (yoneda.map D.W.ι) f g := by
158	  refine IsPullback.of_forall_isPullback_app fun S => ?_
159	  rw [Types.isPullback_iff]
160	  refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩
161	  · exact congrArg (fun φ : yoneda.obj (D.W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1 =>
162	      φ.app S) D.sq
163	  · -- joint injectivity: already forced by `W.ι` alone, being a monomorphism
164	    rintro u₁ u₂ ⟨-, h₂⟩
165	    have : u₁ ≫ D.W.ι = u₂ ≫ D.W.ι := h₂
166	    exact (cancel_mono D.W.ι).mp this
167	  · -- joint surjectivity: `exists_factor` at the test `S.unop`
168	    intro v w hvw
169	    obtain ⟨u, hu₁, hu₂⟩ := D.exists_factor S.unop v w hvw
170	    exact ⟨u, hu₁, hu₂⟩
171	
172	end ChartFibrePresented
173	
174	/-- **THE CRITERION** — `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` from elementwise data, discharging BOTH
175	clauses of `MorphismProperty.relative` at once.
176	
177	Given, for every test point of the target sheaf, a `ChartFibrePresented` datum, the chart map
178	is an open immersion of presheaves.  Certificate-free, divRep-free, and with no reference to
179	divisors: the input is a family of opens of tests together with the coverage statement on
180	each.
181	
182	This is the honest shape of `IsChartUniv`'s obligation.  Reading `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf`
183	as a single "relative GAP-2" statement conflates:
184	
185	* **relative representability** — that the fibre product is a scheme at all.  Supplied here
186	  by `W`, an open subscheme of the test, and proved by `ChartFibrePresented.isPullback`;
187	* **the property clause** — that each represented pullback is an open immersion.  Supplied
188	  here by `W.ι` being an open immersion, which is free.
189	
190	What is *not* free, and is the whole mathematical content, is `exists_factor`: a class that
191	agrees with a chart value must come from the locus.  For the Abel chart that is the relative
192	form of DAT-C GAP-2 (uniqueness of the normalized effective representative) fed through the
193	classifier — so the CERT-Σ gate is real, but it gates ONE field of ONE structure rather than
194	the whole certificate. -/
195	theorem isOpenImmersion_presheaf_of_chartFibrePresented {X : Scheme.{u}}
196	    (f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
197	    (D : ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (g : yoneda.obj T ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1),
198	      ChartFibrePresented C f g) :
199	    IsOpenImmersion.presheaf f := by
200	  refine MorphismProperty.relative.of_exists fun T g => ?_
201	  exact ⟨(D T g).W, yoneda.map (D T g).r, (D T g).W.ι, (D T g).isPullback,
202	    inferInstance⟩
203	
204	/-! ## The criterion is not vacuous
205	
206	A structure whose hard field is an existential can be inhabited for trivial reasons, and a
207	criterion built on one is then worthless.  This section rules that out **by proof** rather
208	than by inspection: the datum is unconstructible exactly when it must be. -/
209	
210	/-- **Non-vacuity of `ChartFibrePresented`, from the necessary direction.**
211	
212	If a chart map fails to be injective on the points of even one test, then no family of
213	`ChartFibrePresented` data exists for it.  In particular the criterion cannot be satisfied
214	for the *unrestricted* Abel chart, whose non-injectivity is the linear system `|D|`
215	(`Pic0AtlasFromDivRep.lean:54`): the criterion's hypothesis is genuinely as strong as the
216	conclusion, and `exists_factor` is not a clause one can talk one's way past.
217	
218	The proof composes the two halves of this file, which is the point of having both. -/
219	theorem isEmpty_forall_chartFibrePresented_of_not_injective {X : Scheme.{u}}
220	    (f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1) (T : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ)
221	    (hT : ¬ Function.Injective (f.app T)) :
222	    IsEmpty (∀ (T' : Scheme.{u}) (g : yoneda.obj T' ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1),
223	        ChartFibrePresented C f g) :=
224	  ⟨fun D => hT (injective_of_isOpenImmersion_presheaf
225	    (isOpenImmersion_presheaf_of_chartFibrePresented f D) T)⟩
226	
227	/-- The same statement in the form a lane will meet it: the criterion's input **implies**
228	elementwise injectivity on every test.  So a lane that cannot prove uniqueness of the
229	normalized effective representative cannot supply the datum either — the CERT-Σ gate is not
230	an artefact of how `IsChartUniv` was pinned. -/
231	theorem injective_of_chartFibrePresented {X : Scheme.{u}}
232	    (f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
233	    (D : ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (g : yoneda.obj T ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1),
234	      ChartFibrePresented C f g) (T : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ) :
235	    Function.Injective (f.app T) :=
236	  injective_of_isOpenImmersion_presheaf
237	    (isOpenImmersion_presheaf_of_chartFibrePresented f D) T
238	
239	end
240	
241	end AlgebraicGeometry

1	/-
2	Copyright (c) 2026 The AlgebraicJacobian authors. All rights reserved.
3	Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
4	Authors: The AlgebraicJacobian Contributors
5	-/
6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivisorFamilyZarSheaf
7	
8	/-!
9	# The divisor functor (DD-2 S6b)
10	
11	The one-screen functor packaging of the locally certified divisor vehicle
12	(`informal/spec-dd-2.md` §6, spelling (A) of I-0222, co-signed by the DD-R lane):
13	
14	* `AlgebraicGeometry.divFunctor`: `(Over (Spec k))ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u`, with object values
15	  `divFamZar C π n T` and action `divFamZar.map` — the `picEtFunctor` house pattern.
16	  Type-valued: degree-`n` divisor families carry no group structure.
17	
18	This is the functor `divRep` is stated against (`informal/spec-dd-r.md` §3 item 8,
19	Addendum 1).  The sheaf halves are consumed as-is from
20	`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivisorFamilyZarSheaf` (`ext_of_le_cover` /
21	`existsUnique_glue_of_le_cover`), the pic0/01JJ precedent.
22	-/
23	
24	set_option autoImplicit false
25	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false
26	/- `lake env lean` drops the lakefile's `[leanOptions]` (I-0161), so the pinned synthesis
27	depth must be set in-file for the faithful per-file check. -/
28	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
29	
30	universe u
31	
32	open CategoryTheory
33	
34	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
35	
36	attribute [local instance] Over.sectionsAlgebra Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
37	
38	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
39	variable (π : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsAffineHom π] (n : ℕ)
40	
41	/-- **The divisor functor** (DD-2 S6b, the pinned name): the locally certified
42	degree-`n` divisor families as a presheaf of types on the slice over `Spec k`,
43	with the glued restriction `divFamZar.map` along arbitrary test morphisms — the
44	`picDegLayerFunctor` house pattern. -/
45	noncomputable def divFunctor : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u where
46	  obj T := divFamZar C π n T.unop
47	  map g := ↾divFamZar.map C π n g.unop
48	  map_id T := by
49	    ext s U
50	    exact congrArg (fun z : divFamZar C π n T.unop => z.1 U) (divFamZar.map_id C π n s)
51	  map_comp {T T' T''} g h := by
52	    ext s U
53	    exact congrArg (fun z : divFamZar C π n T''.unop => z.1 U)
54	      (divFamZar.map_comp C π n g.unop h.unop s)
55	
56	@[simp]
57	lemma divFunctor_obj (T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ) :
58	    (divFunctor C π n).obj T = divFamZar C π n T.unop :=
59	  rfl
60	
61	@[simp]
62	lemma divFunctor_map {T T' : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ} (g : T ⟶ T')
63	    (s : divFamZar C π n T.unop) :
64	    (divFunctor C π n).map g s = divFamZar.map C π n g.unop s :=
65	  rfl
66	
67	end AlgebraicGeometry

33	| honesty over the étale carrier | `PicEtAff.map_mk_eq_unit_self` (`Pic0ChartHonest`) | **landed** |
34	| pointwise presentation | `IsChartDatumPresentation` (below) | **HALF landed** (see note) |
35	| `cechPicClass_inv` | the class law of `invDatum` | **NOT landed**, and off the path |
36	
37	(The engine is Noetherian-free; the GAP-1 inverse and the carrier/field translation landed
38	2026-07-28.)
39	
40	**The GAP-1 mul row is struck, and this paragraph is a correction of what stood here.**  It
41	used to say the residue was the shifted-datum presentation and that "producing it needs the
42	mul/tensor half of GAP-1, which needs a common refinement of two basic-open covers".  That is
43	false (`Picard/Pic0ChartTwistCollapse.lean`): the twist is ONE `thetaFamily`, since
44	`sigmaFamily` *is* a `thetaFamily` and `thetaFamily` is multiplicative in its class, so Σ and
45	`θᵐ` fuse in `CechPic` over the fixed base before any datum is extracted; and
46	`exists_cechPicClass_eq` presents an arbitrary class, product or not, outright.
47	
48	**What genuinely remains, stated without under-pricing it** (this is the correction the
49	reviewer of I-0558 asked for).  Two things, and neither is bookkeeping:
50	
51	1. ~~**Honesty over a general affine base.**~~  **LANDED** (`Picard/Pic0ChartHonest.lean`).  This
52	   row read: `exists_datum_cechPicClass_chartTwistClass` takes an honest Čech class `c` over `B`
53	   as a *hypothesis*, and nothing supplies one, because the splitting theorem
54	   (`exists_splitting_of_picEt`) needs `[Field K]` — its engine is étale field-cofinality — and
55	   the only other plus-unit surjectivity is field-only too.  All of that is accurate about the
56	   tree and none of it matters: **a cover splits over its own carrier.**
57	   `PicEtAff.map_mk_eq_unit_self` gives `PicEtAff.map C E.Carrier (mk C E x) = unit C E.Carrier x`
58	   over an ARBITRARY affine base, because the map cofinality was being asked to produce is the
59	   *identity* `E.Carrier →ₐ[A] E.Carrier`.  This is exactly the (b-amendment)'s "over the étale
60	   carrier `B := E.Carrier` the class is honest" step, so it was never a general-`A` obligation
61	   in the first place.
62	2. **The pointwise presentation itself** — now the ONLY residue.  `IsChartDatumPresentation` asks
63	   for ONE datum over
64	   `A` whose fibre predicate matches, at every residue field simultaneously, a split predicate
65	   whose splitting field `L` varies from point to point (`IsSplitWitness` quantifies `L`
66	   existentially *per point*).  Calling that "a `cechPicClass` base-change statement, not a
67	   construction" — as an earlier draft of this header did — prices a construction as
68	   bookkeeping, which is precisely the mis-pricing the twist-collapse retraction was written
69	   to correct one level up.
70	
71	Everything downstream of a presenting datum is landed.
72	
73	**UPDATE 2026-07-28 (`de63abac6`): the residue of row 2 is now HALF discharged, and the half
74	that fell was the one this paragraph did not expect.**
75	`Picard/Pic0ChartPresentationHalf.lean` proves the **forward** direction of
76	`IsChartDatumPresentation` from a hypothesis containing no witness, no `H¹` and no divisor:
77	`IsChartDatumPlusFibre`, which says only that the datum presents `μ` at every residue field *as
78	plus classes*.  The move is to take the splitting extension to be `κ(t)` **itself** — the datum's
79	witness divisor is already in the right class over `κ(t)` with vanishing `H¹`, so nothing needs
80	transporting.  That trivial splitting `L := K` had been recorded as unelaborable (memory I-0564);
81	it is one line since that record's partial retraction (see
82	`isSplitWitness_of_presenting_witness` in `Picard/Pic0ChartTwistSplit.lean`).
83	
84	What is still owed is the **converse**, and the per-point quantification of `L` this paragraph
85	warns about is exactly where it bites: one receives a witness over some `L_t` varying with `t`,
86	lying in `μ`'s class there rather than visibly in `D`'s at `κ(t)`.
87	`isChartDatumPresentation_of_plusFibre_of_converse` assembles the `↔` from the two halves, so a
88	lane closing this row faces one obligation instead of two.
89	
90	## The shape of this file
91	
92	`IsChartDatumPresentation` names exactly that residue as a hypothesis — a *per-field*
93	presentation of the twisted fibre class by a datum — and `isOpen_chartLocus_of_presentation`
94	derives the openness from it over an affine test.  This is the honest factorisation: the
95	theorem is real mathematics (it is the three transports plus the dictionary), and the
96	hypothesis is a single, precisely stated obligation.  (An earlier draft said the GAP-1
97	mul/tensor brick would discharge it; see the struck table row for why that was wrong.)
98	
99	Writing it the other way round — stating `isOpen_chartLocus` unconditionally with a `sorry`
100	— would hide the fact that the missing input is a *construction*, not a proof.
101	
102	**This file is sorry-free as of 2026-07-28.**  Its earlier single `sorry` (the carrier/field
103	translation) was not a mathematical gap: it was an artifact of taking the `Algebra A` /
104	`IsScalarTower k A` structures on `κ(t)` as explicit `alg`/`tow` *arguments*, which both made
105	the statement FALSE for some regradings — `HasWitnessH1Vanishing` reads its `Algebra` instance
106	inside `relCurveMap C B L`, so a non-canonical `alg` names a different base-change map and a
107	different set — and forced every consumer to carry two dead parameters.  (No refuting
108	`A`, `alg` was exhibited, so the honest verdict is "wrong shape, false for some regradings",
109	not "no proof can exist"; recorded per I-0559.)  With the canonical
110	instances of `Picard/Pic0ChartTestPoint.lean` the whole translation is
111	`hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_of_fieldExtension` across `Spec.residueFieldIso`, and the carrier
112	identification `↥(overSpec k A).left = PrimeSpectrum A` is definitional.  The general lesson
113	is recorded on the `chart-u` roadmap node.
114	
115	## Main declarations
116	
117	* `AlgebraicGeometry.IsChartDatumPresentation` — the residue, named.
118	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartLocus_eq_cechWitnessLocus_of_presentation` — the identification of
119	  `chartLocus` over an affine test with the landed class-indexed witness locus.  This is
120	  transports (0) and (iii) discharged.
121	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isOpen_chartLocus_of_presentation` — **the keystone, conditionally**:
122	  `chartLocus` is open over an affine test given the presentation.
123	-/

142	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
143	attribute [local instance 10000] relCurve.instOver

145	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
146	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite π]
147	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
148	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]

152	/-! ## The residue of the chain, named -/
153	
154	variable (C π) in
155	/-- **The shifted-datum presentation hypothesis** — the one link of the CHART-U(b) route of
156	record that is not landed, stated exactly.
157	
158	Over an affine test `Spec A`, for a class `μ : picEt C (overSpec k A)` (in practice the
159	twisted family `chartTwist C m Z _ λ` restricted to the test), a presentation is a
160	`BasicOpenCocycleDatum` over `A` whose fibre witness predicate at every residue field agrees
161	with the split witness predicate of `μ` at the corresponding point.
162	
163	Two remarks on the shape, both deliberate:
164	
165	* it is stated as an **agreement of predicates at every point**, not as a class equality.
166	  That is weaker than "the datum's class is `μ`", and it is all the openness argument
167	  consumes — which matters, because the class equality is what needs `cechPicClass_inv` and
168	  a class-level identification, whereas a lane that can produce the pointwise agreement by any
169	  other route may use this theorem immediately;
170	* the split predicate is read at `Over.testPoint`, i.e. at the canonical residue-field point
171	  of the affine test, so no choice of affine chart enters;
172	* the `Algebra A (testPointField t)` / `IsScalarTower k A (testPointField t)` instances the
173	  datum predicate needs are the **canonical** ones of `Picard/Pic0ChartTestPoint.lean`.  An
174	  earlier draft of this file carried them as explicit `alg`/`tow` arguments; that was strictly
175	  worse — it made the statement false for some regradings (`HasWitnessH1Vanishing` reads its
176	  `Algebra` instance inside `relCurveMap`, so a non-canonical `alg` names a different set) as
177	  well as unusable. -/
178	def IsChartDatumPresentation {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
179	    (μ : picEt C (overSpec k A)) (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C A π) : Prop :=
180	  ∀ t : (overSpec k A).left,
181	    D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t)
182	      ↔ IsSplitWitness C (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) μ)
183	
184	/-! ## The carrier translation: `testPointField` on `Spec A` versus `Ideal.ResidueField`
185	
186	The engine's open set lives in `PrimeSpectrum A` and is indexed by `q.asIdeal.ResidueField`;
187	`chartLocus` lives in `(overSpec k A).left = Spec A` and is indexed by `Over.testPointField`.
188	The two carriers are the same space, but the two *fields* are only canonically isomorphic
189	(mathlib's `Spec.residueFieldIso`), so the witness predicate has to be carried across that
190	isomorphism.  That is what this section does, and it is the transport the (b-amendment) folds
191	into "affine pieces glue by (V1c)-style locality". -/
192	
193	/-- **The residue-field comparison at a point of an affine test, as an algebra map.**
194	
195	`Over.testPointField t` is the *scheme* residue field `(Spec A).residueField t`, while every
196	engine-facing predicate reads the *algebraic* residue field `t.asIdeal.ResidueField` of the
197	prime.  Mathlib's `Spec.residueFieldIso` identifies them; this records the identification in
198	the form the tower needs, namely that the canonical `A`-algebra structure on the scheme
199	residue field (`Over.instAlgebraTestPointFieldAffine`) factors through the algebraic one.
200	
201	Proof: both sides are `Spec.preimage` of a morphism out of `Spec κ(t)`, and `Spec.map` is
202	injective on homs, so it suffices to compare after applying `Spec.map` — where the identity is
203	mathlib's `Spec.map_residueFieldIso_inv_eq_fromSpecResidueField`. -/
204	lemma algebraMap_testPointFieldAffine_factors {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
205	    (t : (overSpec k A).left) :
206	    algebraMap A (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t)
207	      = ((Scheme.Spec.residueFieldIso (.of A) t).inv).hom.comp
208	          (algebraMap A (t : PrimeSpectrum A).asIdeal.ResidueField) := by
209	  rw [Over.algebraMap_testPointFieldAffine]
210	  have h : Spec.preimage ((overSpec k A).left.fromSpecResidueField t)
211	      = CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A (t : PrimeSpectrum A).asIdeal.ResidueField)
212	          ≫ (Scheme.Spec.residueFieldIso (.of A) t).inv := by
213	    apply Spec.map_injective
214	    rw [Spec.map_preimage, Spec.map_comp]
215	    exact (Scheme.Spec.map_residueFieldIso_inv_eq_fromSpecResidueField (.of A) t).symm
216	  rw [h]
217	  rfl
218	
219	/-- **The witness predicate at a scheme-residue field agrees with the one at the prime's
220	residue field, and the resulting locus is open.**
221	
222	`Over.testPointField t` is `(Spec A).residueField t` and the engine reads
223	`t.asIdeal.ResidueField`; `Spec.residueFieldIso` identifies them, and the witness predicate
224	transfers along any field extension in the `A`-tower
225	(`hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_of_fieldExtension`, `Pic0ChartLocusFibreField.lean:142`), in
226	particular along an isomorphism.
227	
228	Three points about the proof, each of which was a suspected wall and is not:
229	
230	* the **carrier identification** `↥(overSpec k A).left = PrimeSpectrum A` is *definitional*
231	  (`Scheme.Spec`'s carrier is `PrimeSpectrum` on the nose), so the two index sets need no
232	  transport and the two topologies agree by `rfl`.  The set equality below is therefore a
233	  pointwise `Iff`, not a homeomorphism argument;
234	* the `Algebra A (testPointField t)` and `IsScalarTower k A (testPointField t)` instances the
235	  predicate needs are **already canonical** (`Over.instAlgebraTestPointFieldAffine`,
236	  `Over.instIsScalarTowerTestPointFieldAffine`), so nothing has to be passed in as an
237	  argument.  An earlier draft of this file took `alg`/`tow` as explicit hypotheses and left
238	  the conclusion as a `sorry`; that was a statement-shape artifact, not a gap — and worse,
239	  the hypothesis form is *false for some regradings*, since an arbitrary `alg` need not be the
240	  canonical instance and the predicate is not invariant under regrading the field over `A`;
241	* the only genuine content is the transport across `Spec.residueFieldIso`, which is
242	  `hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_of_fieldExtension` applied to the isomorphism, in the tower
243	  `A → κ(q) → (Spec A).residueField t` supplied by
244	  `algebraMap_testPointFieldAffine_factors`. -/
245	theorem isOpen_setOf_hasWitnessH1Vanishing_testPointField
246	    (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom) {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
247	    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C A π) :
248	    IsOpen {t : (overSpec k A).left |
249	      D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t)} := by
250	  -- The two loci are the SAME set of the SAME type: `↥(overSpec k A).left` is
251	  -- `PrimeSpectrum A` definitionally, so only the fibre field differs, and the predicate is
252	  -- invariant under the isomorphism between the two readings of it.
253	  have hset : {t : (overSpec k A).left |
254	        D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t)}
255	      = {q : PrimeSpectrum A |
256	          ∃ W : ((C ⊗ overSpec k q.asIdeal.ResidueField).left).CurveDivisor,
257	            Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass q.asIdeal.ResidueField W
258	                = Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C A q.asIdeal.ResidueField)
259	                    D.cechPicClass
260	              ∧ Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule
261	                  ((C ⊗ overSpec k q.asIdeal.ResidueField).left.divisorSheaf
262	                    q.asIdeal.ResidueField W) 1)} := by
263	    refine Set.ext fun t => ?_
264	    -- the comparison iso as an algebra structure, and its tower over `A`
265	    letI : Algebra (t : PrimeSpectrum A).asIdeal.ResidueField
266	        (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) :=
267	      ((Scheme.Spec.residueFieldIso (.of A) t).inv).hom.toAlgebra
268	    haveI : IsScalarTower A (t : PrimeSpectrum A).asIdeal.ResidueField
269	        (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) :=
270	      IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq' (algebraMap_testPointFieldAffine_factors t)
271	    exact (D.hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_of_fieldExtension
272	      (t : PrimeSpectrum A).asIdeal.ResidueField
273	      (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t)).symm
274	  rw [hset]
275	  exact D.isOpen_setOf_exists_witness_h1_vanishing hπ
276	
277	/-! ## Transports (0) and (iii): the identification with the landed locus -/
278	
279	/-- **`chartLocus` over an affine test is the witness locus of a presenting datum.**
280	
281	This is transport (0) (the class-indexation, landed as `cechWitnessLocus`) composed with
282	transport (iii) (locality on the affine test, here trivial because the test *is* affine),
283	run against the presentation hypothesis.  The content is entirely the translation between
284	the two ways the tree indexes a fibre — by a point of the test object's space
285	(`Over.testPoint`, the `chartLocus` side) and by a prime of the test algebra
286	(`q.asIdeal.ResidueField`, the engine side).
287	
288	The translation is available precisely because `Over.testPointField` at a point of
289	`(overSpec k A).left = Spec A` and `q.asIdeal.ResidueField` at the corresponding prime are
290	the same field up to the canonical `Spec.residueFieldIso`, and the witness predicate is
291	invariant under field isomorphism over the base (`hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_of_fieldExtension`
292	applied to an isomorphism). -/
293	theorem mem_chartLocus_iff_hasWitnessH1Vanishing
294	    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
295	    {μ : picEt C (overSpec k A)} {D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C A π}
296	    (hpres : IsChartDatumPresentation C π μ D) (t : (overSpec k A).left) :
297	    IsSplitWitness C (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) μ)
298	      ↔ D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) :=
299	  (hpres t).symm
300	
301	/-! ## The keystone, conditionally -/
302	
303	variable (C π) in
304	/-- **`isOpen_chartLocus`, given the shifted-datum presentation** (dat-b row B-4's keystone,
305	over an affine test).
306	
307	The proof is the route of record with the one missing link supplied as `hpres`: rewrite
308	membership of `chartLocus` as the datum's witness predicate at the residue field of the
309	point (the presentation), then quote the landed datum-level openness
310	`BasicOpenCocycleDatum.isOpen_setOf_exists_witness_h1_vanishing` — itself the engine
311	`datumRigidEngine_isOpen_vanishing` read through the GAP-6 dictionary.
312	
313	The general-test statement follows from this one by the affine-piece locality of the
314	(b-amendment)'s transport (iii): `chartLocus` over `T` meets each affine open `U ⊆ T.left` in
315	`chartLocus` over `Spec Γ(T.left, U)` (by `picEtMap_chartTwist` along
316	`Over.fromSpecAffine T U`), and a set that is open in every member of an open cover is open.
317	That last step is `isOpen_iff_forall_isOpen_inter`-style bookkeeping and needs no new
318	mathematics; it is not stated here only because it would need the presentation hypothesis
319	*per affine piece*, which is a statement about the general test and therefore belongs with
320	the honesty/presentation obligations named in the header table. -/
321	theorem isOpen_setOf_isSplitWitness_of_presentation (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom)
322	    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
323	    {μ : picEt C (overSpec k A)} {D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C A π}
324	    (hpres : IsChartDatumPresentation C π μ D) :
325	    IsOpen {t : (overSpec k A).left |
326	      IsSplitWitness C (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) μ)} := by
327	  -- The engine's open set is indexed by primes of `A`; the locus is indexed by points of
328	  -- `Spec A`.  These carriers are the same type, so the presentation rewrites one into the
329	  -- other pointwise.
330	  have hset : {t : (overSpec k A).left |
331	        IsSplitWitness C (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) μ)}
332	      = {t : (overSpec k A).left |
333	          D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t)} :=
334	    Set.ext fun t => mem_chartLocus_iff_hasWitnessH1Vanishing hpres t
335	  rw [hset]
336	  exact isOpen_setOf_hasWitnessH1Vanishing_testPointField hπ D
337	
338	end

7	
8	/-!
9	# B-5 at the Abel chart: what the pointwise datum unfolds to, and what it costs
10	
11	`Picard/Pic0ChartCoveragePointwise.lean` reduces `ChartsCoverLocally` — hence B-6 — to a
12	four-part datum at each point of each test.  That reduction is stated for an *arbitrary*
13	family of presheaf maps, so it says nothing about how hard the datum is at the family that
14	matters.  This file instantiates it at `abelSigmaChart` and computes the answer.
15	
16	## The computation, and the one thing it makes visible
17	
18	A section of `pic0SigmaSheaf C` over a **bare** test scheme `T` is by definition a *pair*
19	`⟨a, λ⟩` with `a : T ⟶ Spec k` and `λ` a degree-zero class on the slice object `Over.mk a`
20	(`Over.sigmaExtension`, `Picard/OverSigmaExtension.lean`).  And `(Over.mk a).left` is `T`
21	itself, definitionally.  So the big-site/slice crossing that looks like it needs a bridge does
22	not: the pointwise datum's `t : ↥T` *is* a point of the slice test, and `chartLocus` applies to
23	it with no transport.  `abelChartApp_eq` below records the crossing as an equation rather than
24	leaving it to unfold at a use site.
25	
26	What the computation *does* make visible is where the cost sits.  `abelSigmaChart`'s value at
27	`x : W ⟶ D.left` is `⟨x ≫ D.hom, chartValue … (rep.homEquiv …)⟩`, so matching it against the
28	restriction of `⟨a, λ⟩` needs **both** components: the Σ-component is an equation between
29	morphisms to `Spec k`, and only then is there a class equation.  A producer that supplies the
30	class half alone has not supplied the datum — the Σ-component is what pins the chart point to
31	lie *over* the test, and it is free only because `W.ι ≫ a` is what `D.hom` must equal.
32	
33	## THE CORRECTION THIS FILE CARRIES, against this lane's own headline
34	
35	`Pic0ChartUnivReduce.lean:40` says of its `chartLocusOpens`:
36	
37	> `chartLocusOpens` is **constructed**, not hypothesised — the `W` field costs zero, which is
38	> a real reduction of the datum from four fields to three
39	
40	**The second clause is false, and the roadmap `c9b` row repeats it** ("`W` needs nothing").
41	`chartLocusOpens` takes an argument `haff`, the affine-local openness of the locus at every
42	affine open of the test, and *nothing in the tree discharges it*:
43	`isOpen_chartLocus_of_affineLocal'` (`Pic0ChartLocusIsoInvariance.lean`) removed the
44	`IsSplitWitnessIsoInvariant` hypothesis and passes `haff` straight through, as does
45	`isOpen_chartLocus_of_affineLocal` before it.  The affine case that would feed it is
46	`isOpen_setOf_isSplitWitness_of_presentation` (`Pic0ChartLocusIsOpen.lean:321`), which is
47	itself conditional on `IsChartDatumPresentation` — B-4's *named residue*.
48	
49	**Update, same session** (`Picard/Pic0ChartPresentationConverse.lean`): that residue is now
50	*entirely witness-free*.  Its forward half already was (the trivial splitting), and its
51	converse `hconv` — the descent direction, open for three sessions — is discharged by plus-unit
52	injectivity.  So what `haff` ultimately costs is a `cechPicClass` base-change identity: no
53	witness, no `H¹`, no divisor, and nothing certificate- or divRep-gated.
54	
55	So the honest accounting is: **`W` costs `haff`, which costs B-4's presentation residue.**  The
56	datum went from four fields to three *shapes* but not to three *obligations*.  What is
57	genuinely free is the type-level crossing above, and `chartLocusHaff` below is the residue
58	named so it cannot be lost again.
59	
60	## Main declarations
61	
62	* `AlgebraicGeometry.abelChartApp_eq` — the Abel chart's value at a point of the divisor
63	  scheme, as an explicit `Sigma.mk`.  Both components, since the datum needs both.
64	* `AlgebraicGeometry.ChartLocusAffineLocal` — the `haff` residue, named.  This is what
65	  `chartLocusOpens` silently costs.
66	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartLocusOpens_of_affineLocal` — `chartLocusOpens` from it, so the
67	  dependency is explicit in the API rather than in an argument position.
68	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartLocusAffineLocal_of_presentation` — the residue **reduced to B-4's
69	  own named obligation**: a per-affine-piece `IsChartDatumPresentation` gives it.  This is the
70	  link that was asserted in `Pic0ChartLocusIsOpen`'s docstring and never written.
71	-/
72

74	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3

91	/-! ## The Abel chart's value, both components -/
92	
93	/-- **The Abel chart map evaluated at a point of the divisor scheme.**
94	
95	`abelSigmaChart` is `rep.toSigmaExtension ≫ Over.sigmaExtensionNat (chartValueTrans …)`, and
96	both factors act componentwise on the Σ-extension, so the value at `x : Y ⟶ D.left` is the
97	pair whose structure morphism is `x ≫ D.hom` and whose class is the chart value of the divisor
98	family `rep.homEquiv (Over.homMk x rfl)`.
99	
100	Recorded as an equation because a coverage producer has to match this against a *given*
101	section, and the match is two equations rather than one: the Σ-components must agree before
102	the classes are even in the same type.  Leaving it to unfold at the use site is how the
103	Σ-component gets forgotten. -/
104	@[simp]
105	theorem abelChartApp_eq {D : Over (Spec (.of k))} (rep : (divFunctor C π n).RepresentableBy D)
106	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
107	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
108	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (n : ℤ))
109	    (Y : Scheme.{u}) (x : Y ⟶ D.left) :
110	    (abelSigmaChart C π n rep m Z hdeg).app (op Y) x
111	      = ⟨x ≫ D.hom, ⟨chartValue C π n m Z (Over.mk (x ≫ D.hom))
112	          (rep.homEquiv (Over.homMk x rfl)),
113	        chartValue_mem_pic0Subgroup C π n m Z hdeg _ _⟩⟩ :=
114	  rfl
115	
116	/-! ## The `haff` residue, named
117	
118	`chartLocusOpens` takes the affine-local openness as an argument.  Naming it is not cosmetic:
119	an argument in a definition's signature is invisible to a census of open obligations, which is
120	how "the `W` field costs zero" survived into two roadmap rows. -/
121	
122	variable (C) in
123	/-- **The affine-local openness residue of `chartLocus`** — what `chartLocusOpens` costs.
124	
125	For a test `T` and a class `lam` on it, this says the chart locus is open over every affine
126	open piece of `T`.  It is exactly the `haff` argument of `isOpen_chartLocus_of_affineLocal'`,
127	and it is the *only* remaining input to CHART-U(b) at a general test: the iso-invariance
128	hypothesis that used to sit beside it was discharged
129	(`isSplitWitnessIsoInvariant_holds`), but this one was passed through, not proved.
130	
131	Named as a `Prop` so that it appears in searches for open obligations. -/
132	def ChartLocusAffineLocal (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
133	    (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (lam : picEt C T) : Prop :=
134	  ∀ U : T.left.affineOpens,
135	    IsOpen (chartLocus C m Z (picEtMap C (Over.fromSpecAffine T U) lam))
136	
137	variable (C) in
138	/-- `chartLocusOpens` with its cost made explicit in the API.
139	
140	Identical in content to `chartLocusOpens` — the point is that the dependency is now a named
141	`Prop` a reader can grep for, rather than an unnamed argument that reads as bookkeeping. -/
142	def chartLocusOpens' (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
143	    (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (lam : picEt C T)
144	    (haff : ChartLocusAffineLocal C m Z T lam) : T.left.Opens :=
145	  chartLocusOpens C m Z T lam haff
146	
147	@[simp]
148	lemma mem_chartLocusOpens' {m : ℕ} {Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor}
149	    {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} {lam : picEt C T} {haff : ChartLocusAffineLocal C m Z T lam}
150	    {t : T.left} :
151	    t ∈ chartLocusOpens' C m Z T lam haff ↔ t ∈ chartLocus C m Z lam :=
152	  Iff.rfl
153	
154	/-! ## Reducing the residue to B-4's own named obligation
155	
156	`Pic0ChartLocusIsOpen.lean:321`'s docstring says the general-test statement follows from the
157	affine one "by the affine-piece locality of the (b-amendment)'s transport (iii)", and adds that
158	it "is not stated here only because it would need the presentation hypothesis *per affine
159	piece*".  That is right, and this is the statement it describes. -/
160	
161	set_option linter.overlappingInstances false in
162	variable (C π) in
163	/-- **The `haff` residue from a per-affine-piece presentation** — the link
164	`Pic0ChartLocusIsOpen`'s docstring describes and does not state.
165	
166	For each affine open `U` of the test, a `BasicOpenCocycleDatum` over `Γ(T.left, U)` presenting
167	the restricted twisted class gives openness of the locus on that piece
168	(`isOpen_setOf_isSplitWitness_of_presentation`), and `chartLocus` over the piece *is* that set
169	by definition (`chartLocus` unfolds to the split-witness set of the twisted class, and the
170	twist commutes with restriction by `picEtMap_chartTwist`).
171	
172	So the affine-local residue is **exactly** B-4's presentation obligation, quantified over
173	affine pieces — no extra geometry, and in particular nothing certificate- or divRep-gated.
174	Combined with `isOpen_chartLocus_of_affineLocal'` this closes CHART-U(b) at a general test the
175	moment `IsChartDatumPresentation` is available per piece.
176	
177	The `hπ` and `IsFinite π` hypotheses are the ones
178	`isOpen_setOf_isSplitWitness_of_presentation` carries.  `IsFinite π` is strictly stronger than
179	the file-level `IsAffineHom π` (whence the overlapping-instance warning, disabled below): the
180	affine openness route runs through the rigid engine, which needs finiteness, while the rest of
181	this file needs only affineness. -/
182	theorem chartLocusAffineLocal_of_presentation [IsFinite π]
183	    (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom)
184	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
185	    (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (lam : picEt C T)
186	    (hpres : ∀ U : T.left.affineOpens,
187	      ∃ D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C (Γ(T.left, U.1)) π,
188	        IsChartDatumPresentation C π
189	          (chartTwist C m Z _ (picEtMap C (Over.fromSpecAffine T U) lam)) D) :
190	    ChartLocusAffineLocal C m Z T lam := by
191	  intro U
192	  obtain ⟨D, hD⟩ := hpres U
193	  exact isOpen_setOf_isSplitWitness_of_presentation C π hπ hD
194	
195	end
196	
197	end AlgebraicGeometry

6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivRepAffKit
7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivisorFamilyZarFunctor
8	
9	/-!
10	# Conditional final packaging of divisor representability
11	
12	DDR-9.F7 has two logically separate parts: lifting the affine equivalences to arbitrary
13	tests, and packaging the resulting natural equivalences as a `RepresentableBy` datum.
14	This file formalizes the second part.  `DivRepGlobalData` records the general-test
15	pullback, classification map, inverse laws, and naturality.  Its `representableBy`
16	constructor is the final categorical packaging.
17	
18	The affine-to-general lift is intentionally not assumed to exist implicitly: a caller
19	must provide every field of `DivRepGlobalData`.
20	-/
21	
22	set_option autoImplicit false
23	set_option quotPrecheck false
24	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false
25	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
26	
27	universe u
28	
29	open CategoryTheory
30	
31	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
32	
33	open Grassmannian Scheme
34	
35	section Curve
36	
37	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))}
38	variable {pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite pi]
39	
40	noncomputable local instance instOverCleftDivRepKit :
41	    C.left.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) := ⟨C.hom⟩
42	
43	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (C.left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))]
44	  [IsIntegral C.left]
45	  [LocallyOfFiniteType (C.left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))]
46	  [QuasiCompact (C.left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))]
47	  [IsDominant pi]
48	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
49	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
50	variable [Module.Finite k (Sheaf.HModule (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) 0)]
51	  [Module.Finite k (Sheaf.HModule (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) 1)]
52	variable (hpi : pi ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))
53	variable (g r1 r2 : ℕ)
54	variable (b1 : Module.Basis (Fin r1) k
55	  ↥(divisorSections k (windowM_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi) ⊤))
56	variable (b2 : Module.Basis (Fin r2) k
57	  ↥(divisorSections k
58	    ((windowM_choice pi hpi g + windowS_choice pi hpi g) • fiberWeilDivisor pi) ⊤))
59	
60	local notation "DivOver" =>
61	  divSchemeOver k (windowS_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi)
62	    (windowM_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi) g r1 r2 b1
63	    (b2.map (windowShiftEquiv hpi g).symm)
64	
65	/-- The exact general-test data needed for the final F7 packaging.  In the intended
66	construction, `pull` is assembled from the affine forward maps and `classify` by
67	gluing the affine backward classifiers. -/
68	structure DivRepGlobalData where
69	  pull : ∀ {T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))},
70	    (T ⟶ DivOver) → divFamZar C pi g T
71	  classify : ∀ {T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))},
72	    divFamZar C pi g T → (T ⟶ DivOver)
73	  classify_pull : ∀ {T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))} (v : T ⟶ DivOver),
74	    classify (pull v) = v
75	  pull_classify : ∀ {T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))} (F : divFamZar C pi g T),
76	    pull (classify F) = F
77	  pull_comp : ∀ {T T' : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))} (f : T' ⟶ T)
78	    (v : T ⟶ DivOver),
79	    pull (f ≫ v) = divFamZar.map C pi g f (pull v)
80	
81	namespace DivRepGlobalData
82	
83	/-- The general-test equivalence underlying the represented functor. -/
84	noncomputable def equiv
85	    (D : DivRepGlobalData hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2)
86	    (T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) :
87	    (T ⟶ DivOver) ≃ divFamZar C pi g T where
88	  toFun := D.pull
89	  invFun := D.classify
90	  left_inv := D.classify_pull
91	  right_inv := D.pull_classify
92	
93	set_option linter.unusedSectionVars false in
94	@[simp]
95	theorem equiv_apply
96	    (D : DivRepGlobalData hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2)
97	    {T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))} (v : T ⟶ DivOver) :
98	    equiv (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2) (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) D T v
99	      = D.pull v :=
100	  rfl
101	
102	set_option linter.unusedSectionVars false in
103	@[simp]
104	theorem equiv_symm_apply
105	    (D : DivRepGlobalData hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2)
106	    {T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))} (F : divFamZar C pi g T) :
107	    (equiv (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2) (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) D T).symm F
108	      = D.classify F :=
109	  rfl
110	
111	/-- The final F7 categorical packaging: natural general-test pullback equivalences
112	represent the locally certified divisor functor by `DivScheme`. -/
113	noncomputable def representableBy
114	    (D : DivRepGlobalData hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2) :
115	    (divFunctor C pi g).RepresentableBy DivOver where
116	  homEquiv {T} :=
117	    equiv (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2) (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) D T
118	  homEquiv_comp {T T'} f v := by
119	    change D.pull (f ≫ v) = divFamZar.map C pi g f (D.pull v)
120	    exact D.pull_comp f v
121	
122	set_option linter.unusedSectionVars false in
123	@[simp]
124	theorem representableBy_homEquiv_apply
125	    (D : DivRepGlobalData hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2)
126	    {T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))} (v : T ⟶ DivOver) :
127	    (representableBy (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2) (b1 := b1)
128	      (b2 := b2) D).homEquiv v = D.pull v :=
129	  rfl
130	
131	set_option linter.unusedSectionVars false in
132	@[simp]
133	theorem representableBy_homEquiv_symm_apply
134	    (D : DivRepGlobalData hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2)
135	    {T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))} (F : divFamZar C pi g T) :
136	    (representableBy (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2) (b1 := b1)
137	      (b2 := b2) D).homEquiv.symm F = D.classify F :=
138	  rfl
139	
140	end DivRepGlobalData
141	
142	end Curve
143	
144	end AlgebraicGeometry

8	/-!
9	# U2 as an equation between morphisms: the chart maps lie in the range of the classifier
10	
11	`Picard/DivRepAffPullClause.lean` reduced the whole divisor-representability chain to a
12	single hypothesis, `DivRepChartFamily.IsChartClause U`, and `IsChartClause.of_id` showed
13	that its `ω`-quantifier collapses to the identity point, i.e. to the DDR9-U ε-identity as
14	`informal/w4-ddr9-worksheet.md` §3.1 states it.  That is still a *submodule* identity with
15	a `∀`-quantifier over tower tests and framings hidden inside `IsDivRepClassify`.
16	
17	This file removes that quantifier.  The backward classifier `divRepClassifyZar`
18	(`Picard/DivRepClassifyZar.lean`) is defined for **every** locally certified class over
19	**every** affine test, unconditionally, and `isDivRepClassify_unique` says it is the
20	*only* morphism satisfying the clause.  So the clause is not an extra property at all:
21	
22	> `IsDivRepClassify F₀ v` ↔ `(divRepClassifyZar … F₀).left = v`.
23	
24	Both directions are one line — forward is uniqueness, backward is a rewrite — and the
25	consequence is that U2 becomes an **equation between two morphisms of schemes that both
26	already exist**:
27	
28	> U2 ↔ for each pair chart `(i, j)`, `(divRepClassifyZar … (U i j)).left = ChartMap i j`.
29	
30	Reading off the existential, the last obligation of divisor representability is that
31	each chart map lies in the **range** of the classifier at its own chart ring:
32	
33	> `divFunctor_representableBy_of_chartRange` :
34	>   `(∀ i j, ∃ F, (divRepClassifyZar … F).left = ChartMap i j) →`
35	>   `(divFunctor C π g).RepresentableBy DivOver`
36	
37	Since `divRepClassifyZar` is injective on classes (`eq_of_isDivRepClassify`,
38	`Picard/DivRepClassifyZarSep.lean`), representability of `divFunctor` is *equivalent* to
39	surjectivity of `divRepClassifyZar` at every affine test; what this file records is that
40	surjectivity at the **chart rings alone** suffices.  That is the honest content: the
41	classifier is already a bijection onto its range everywhere, and the whole remaining debt
42	is that the finitely many chart points are hit.
43	
44	## Main declarations
45	
46	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isDivRepClassify_iff_divRepClassifyZar_left_eq` — the clause **is**
47	  the classifier equation, in both directions.  General: no chart family, no universal
48	  point.
49	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivRepChartFamily.isChartClause_iff_forall_classify_eq` — U2 as a
50	  per-chart equation of morphisms, **as an iff**, so it is a reduction and not merely a
51	  restatement (the safeguard of inbox `I-0571`).
52	* `AlgebraicGeometry.divFunctor_representableBy_of_chartRange` — divisor
53	  representability from range membership of the chart maps.
54	
55	## What this does NOT do
56	
57	It produces no class over a chart ring, so it clears no gate: U2 is unproved and, per
58	roadmap `…divrep.u2`, the production of a chart class with the tautological ε remains the
59	G-4 obligation.  What changes is what a producer has to exhibit — a class whose classifier
60	*is* the chart map, rather than a family satisfying a quantified submodule identity.  The
61	endpoint also still carries `hO`, `hχ` and the ambient curve instances.
62	-/

168	-- Both directions instantiate `IsDivRepClassify` at the chart ring, whose `DivCarveChartRing`
169	-- quotient type the elaborator unfolds while unifying `divRepPullAt`'s `mapAlgHom`; the same

172	/-- **U2, as an equation between morphisms** — and an **iff**, so it is a reduction of the
173	obligation rather than a restatement of it (the safeguard of inbox `I-0571`).

175	`IsChartClause U` holds exactly when, for each pair chart `(i, j)`, the backward
176	classifier of the supplied chart class *is* that chart's own map to `DivScheme`.  The
177	`ω`-quantifier collapses by `IsChartClause.of_id`, and the clause at the identity point is
178	the classifier equation by `isDivRepClassify_iff_divRepClassifyZar_left_eq`.

180	So the DDR9-U ε-identity carries no residual quantifier over tower tests or framings: what
181	a producer owes is that two morphisms `Spec R_Z(i,j) ⟶ DivScheme g`, both of which already
182	exist unconditionally, agree. -/
183	theorem isChartClause_iff_forall_classify_eq
184	    (U : ∀ (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J),
185	      DivFamZar C (ChartRing i j) pi g) :
186	    IsChartClause (hpi := hpi) g r1 r2 b1 b2 U ↔
187	      ∀ (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J),
188	        (divRepClassifyZar hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 (ChartRing i j) (U i j)).left
189	          = ChartMap i j := by
190	  refine ⟨fun hU i j => ?_, fun hU => IsChartClause.of_id hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 fun i j => ?_⟩
191	  · -- instantiate the clause at the identity point of the chart
192	    have h := hU (S := ChartRing i j) i j (AlgHom.id k (ChartRing i j))
193	    rw [divRepPullAt_id] at h
194	    -- `Spec` of the identity algebra map is the identity; the rewrite is done at an
195	    -- ABSTRACT algebra (`specMap_ofHom_algHom_id`) because the same step spelled inline
196	    -- against the chart ring's quotient type does not elaborate.
197	    rw [specMap_ofHom_algHom_id (k := k), Category.id_comp] at h
198	    exact (isDivRepClassify_iff_divRepClassifyZar_left_eq hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2
199	      (U i j) (ChartMap i j)).mp h
200	  · exact (isDivRepClassify_iff_divRepClassifyZar_left_eq hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2
201	      (U i j) (ChartMap i j)).mpr (hU i j)
202

208	/-- **Divisor representability from range membership of the chart maps** — the form this
209	file exists to state.

211	`divRepClassifyZar` is injective on classes (`eq_of_isDivRepClassify`), so representability
212	of `divFunctor` is *equivalent* to the classifier being surjective at every affine test.
213	This says surjectivity at the **chart rings alone** suffices: if each chart map
214	`ChartMap i j` is the classifier of *some* locally certified class over its own chart ring
215	`R_Z(i,j)`, then `divFunctor C π g` is represented by `divSchemeOver`.

218	The value is the shape of what is owed: a *preimage under a landed map*, at
219	`glueData`-many points, rather than a quantified submodule identity. -/
220	noncomputable def divFunctor_representableBy_of_chartRange
221	    (hrange : ∀ (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J),
222	      ∃ F : DivFamZar C (ChartRing i j) pi g,
223	        (divRepClassifyZar hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 (ChartRing i j) F).left
224	          = ChartMap i j) :

226	  divFunctor_representableBy_of_chartClause hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2

9	/-!
10	# `IsSplitWitnessIsoInvariant` DISCHARGED — CHART-U(b) at a general test, unconditionally
11	
12	`Picard/Pic0ChartLocusGeneralTest.lean` proves CHART-U(b) over a general test *modulo one
13	hypothesis*: `IsSplitWitnessIsoInvariant C`, the transport of `IsSplitWitness` along an
14	**isomorphism** of reading fields.  That was the single input standing between the landed
15	affine openness and `isOpen_chartLocus` over a general test, and its own docstring priced it as
16	"`PicEtAff.map_map` plus `map_id`, not geometry".
17	
18	**This file proves it, and the price was almost that.**  The route is:
19	
20	1. the residue-field extension a morphism of tests induces is a `k`-algebra map
21	   (`Over.testPointFieldMap_comp_algebraMap`) — this was *not* recorded anywhere, and it is what
22	   lets the extension be read as an `AlgHom`/`AlgEquiv` at all.  It is `Spec.preimage` applied to
23	   the naturality square `Over.testPoint_comp_left`, plus the two `Over` triangles;
24	2. an invertible extension is therefore a `k`-algebra **equivalence**
25	   (`Over.testPointFieldAlgEquiv`);
26	3. `IsSplitWitness` is invariant along such an equivalence
27	   (`isSplitWitness_map_overSpecMap_iff`);
28	4. the naturality square in the `overSpecMap` spelling (`Over.testPoint_comp`) turns (3) into
29	   `IsSplitWitnessIsoInvariant`.
30	
31	## What step (3) actually costs, and where the prediction was right
32	
33	The prediction was `map_map` + `map_id`; what it *is* is `PicEtAff.map_map` in the
34	`mapAlg`-into-a-common-target form (`PicEtAff.map_mapAlg_eq_map`) plus
35	`picEtAffineEquiv_naturality`, and the witness clause is carried through untouched.  So the class
36	side is indeed pure functoriality.
37	
38	**What the prediction did not mention is the instance side, and that is the real content.**
39	`IsSplitWitness C μ` existentially quantifies a splitting field `L` *together with seven
40	instances*, four of them about `L` over the reading field: `Algebra K L`, `IsScalarTower k K L`,
41	`Module.Finite K L`, `Algebra.IsSeparable K L`.  Transporting the predicate along `e : K ≃ₐ[k] K'`
42	keeps **the same `L`** but must re-derive all four over `K'`, along `e.symm`.  Two of them are
43	mathlib transports found by name (`Module.Finite.of_equiv_equiv`,
44	`Algebra.IsSeparable.of_equiv_equiv`, both stated for exactly this square) and two are
45	`IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq`.  A one-line `rw` this is not; but it is bookkeeping, and no
46	geometry enters — in particular nothing about the curve, the twist, or `H¹` is touched.
47	
48	## Why the forward direction genuinely needs an EQUIVALENCE, not an `AlgHom`
49	
50	`isSplitWitness_map_overSpecMap` is stated for `e : K ≃ₐ[k] K'` and the `≃` is load-bearing at a
51	precise point: the transported `Algebra K' L` is `algebraMap K L ∘ e.symm`, which needs `e`
52	*surjective*.  Along a non-invertible `K → K'` there is no `K'`-algebra structure on the old `L`
53	at all, and one would have to base-change `L` — which is the separable-extension route
54	(`exists_witness_of_separable_extension`), a different and strictly harder lemma.  So the `IsIso`
55	hypothesis of `IsSplitWitnessIsoInvariant` is not packaging; it is what makes the same `L` work.
56	
57	## Main declarations
58	
59	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Over.testPointFieldMap_comp_algebraMap` — the induced residue-field
60	  extension is a `k`-algebra map.
61	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Over.testPointFieldAlgHom` / `Over.testPointFieldAlgEquiv` — that extension
62	  as an `AlgHom`, and as an `AlgEquiv` when it is invertible.
63	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Over.testPoint_comp` — the `Pic0ChartTestPoint` naturality square as an
64	  equality of morphisms **in the slice**, through `Over.overSpecMap`.
65	* `AlgebraicGeometry.PicEtAff.map_mapAlg_eq_map` — `map_map` in the form this needs: an explicit
66	  `k`-algebra map into a common target is absorbed by `PicEtAff.map`.
67	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isSplitWitness_map_overSpecMap_iff` — `IsSplitWitness` is invariant along a
68	  `k`-algebra equivalence of the reading field.
69	* **`AlgebraicGeometry.isSplitWitnessIsoInvariant_holds`** — the hypothesis of
70	  `Pic0ChartLocusGeneralTest`, discharged.
71	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartLocus_fromSpecAffine_eq_preimage'`,
72	  `AlgebraicGeometry.isOpen_chartLocus_of_affineLocal'` — the general-test statements with the
73	  hypothesis removed.  **`isOpen_chartLocus_of_affineLocal'` is CHART-U(b) at a general test with
74	  no residue**, which is what `c9b` consumes as the `V` of `restrictChart`.
75	-/

95	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}

104	/-! ## The residue-field extension is a `k`-algebra map
105	
106	`testPointFieldMap` is defined as a bare `CommRingCat` morphism (`Scheme.Hom.residueFieldMap`),
107	and `Pic0ChartTestPoint` records only its `Algebra` reading via `testPointFieldAlgebra`, which
108	makes `κ(t)` a `κ(f t)`-algebra *without* saying anything about `k`.  For the plus-class
109	transport that is not enough: `PicEtAff.mapAlg` consumes a `k`-**algebra** map, so the fact that
110	the extension is one over `k` has to be proved.  It is exactly the two `Over` triangles read
111	through `Spec.preimage`. -/
112	
113	/-- **The residue-field extension induced by a morphism of tests is a `k`-algebra map.**
114	
115	`testPointFieldMap f t : κ(f t) → κ(t)` commutes with the two `k`-algebra structures of
116	`Pic0ChartTestPoint`, both of which are `Spec.preimage` of a composite down to `Spec k`.  The
117	proof is the naturality square `testPoint_comp_left` composed with `T.hom`, pushed through
118	`Spec.preimage` (a bijection on homs out of an affine, so it turns the commuting square of
119	schemes into the commuting square of rings). -/
120	theorem testPointFieldMap_comp_algebraMap {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))} (f : T' ⟶ T)
121	    (t : T'.left) :
122	    (testPointFieldMap f t).hom.comp
123	        (algebraMap k (testPointField (T := T) (f.left.base t)))
124	      = algebraMap k (testPointField (T := T') t) := by
125	  have hw : (testPoint t).left ≫ T'.hom
126	      = Spec.map (testPointFieldMap f t)
127	          ≫ ((testPoint (T := T) (f.left.base t)).left ≫ T.hom) := by
128	    rw [← Category.assoc, ← testPoint_comp_left f t, Category.assoc, Over.w f,
129	      Over.w (testPoint t)]
130	  have hpre := congrArg (fun g => (Spec.preimage g).hom) hw
131	  simp only [Spec.preimage_comp, Spec.preimage_map, CommRingCat.hom_comp] at hpre
132	  exact hpre.symm
133	
134	/-- The residue-field extension at a point, as a `k`-algebra map. -/
135	def testPointFieldAlgHom {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))} (f : T' ⟶ T) (t : T'.left) :
136	    testPointField (T := T) (f.left.base t) →ₐ[k] testPointField (T := T') t :=
137	  { (testPointFieldMap f t).hom with
138	    commutes' := fun r => congrFun (congrArg DFunLike.coe
139	      (testPointFieldMap_comp_algebraMap f t)) r }
140	
141	/-- **An invertible residue-field extension is a `k`-algebra equivalence.**  This is the shape
142	the `IsSplitWitness` transport consumes, and the `IsIso` hypothesis of
143	`IsSplitWitnessIsoInvariant` exists precisely to supply it. -/
144	def testPointFieldAlgEquiv {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))} (f : T' ⟶ T) (t : T'.left)
145	    [IsIso (testPointFieldMap f t)] :
146	    testPointField (T := T) (f.left.base t) ≃ₐ[k] testPointField (T := T') t :=
147	  { (asIso (testPointFieldMap f t)).commRingCatIsoToRingEquiv with
148	    commutes' := (testPointFieldAlgHom f t).commutes }
149	
150	/-- **The naturality square of the bridge, in the slice.**  `Pic0ChartTestPoint.testPoint_comp_left`
151	states it for the underlying scheme morphisms; every class-level transport needs it for the
152	`Over`-morphisms themselves, since `picEtMap` is indexed by those.  Faithfulness of
153	`Over.forget` (`Over.OverMorphism.ext`) is the whole content. -/
154	theorem testPoint_comp {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))} (f : T' ⟶ T) (t : T'.left) :
155	    testPoint t ≫ f
156	      = overSpecMap (testPointFieldAlgHom f t) ≫ testPoint (T := T) (f.left.base t) :=
157	  Over.OverMorphism.ext (by
158	    rw [Over.comp_left, Over.comp_left, Over.overSpecMap_left]
159	    exact testPoint_comp_left f t)
160	
161	end Over

165	omit [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] in
166	/-- **`map_map` in the form the transport needs**: an explicit `k`-algebra map `e : K → K'` that
167	is compatible with two towers into a common `L` is absorbed by `PicEtAff.map`.
168	
169	`PicEtAff.map_map` is stated for a chain of `Algebra` instances; here the middle step is an
170	explicit `AlgHom`, so the `Algebra K K'` it needs is manufactured from `e` and the
171	`IsScalarTower K K' L` from `halg`.  This is the class-side half of the whole iso-invariance,
172	and it is pure functoriality — no field, separability or finiteness hypothesis appears. -/
173	theorem map_mapAlg_eq_map {K K' L : Type u} [CommRing K] [Algebra k K]
174	    [CommRing K'] [Algebra k K'] [CommRing L] [Algebra k L]
175	    [Algebra K L] [Algebra K' L] [IsScalarTower k K L] [IsScalarTower k K' L]
176	    (e : K →ₐ[k] K') (halg : ∀ x : K, algebraMap K' L (e x) = algebraMap K L x)
177	    (a : PicEtAff C K) :
178	    PicEtAff.map C L (PicEtAff.mapAlg C e a) = PicEtAff.map C L a :=
179	  letI : Algebra K K' := e.toRingHom.toAlgebra
180	  haveI : IsScalarTower k K K' := .of_algebraMap_eq fun x => (e.commutes x).symm
181	  haveI : IsScalarTower K K' L := .of_algebraMap_eq fun x => (halg x).symm
182	  PicEtAff.map_map C K' L a
183	
184	end PicEtAff

186	/-! ## Iso-invariance of the split predicate -/
187	
188	variable (C) in
189	/-- **`IsSplitWitness` transports along a `k`-algebra equivalence of the reading field**
190	(forward direction).
191	
192	The splitting field `L` is **not changed**: along `e : K ≃ₐ[k] K'` the same `L` presents the
193	transported class, via the `K'`-algebra structure `algebraMap K L ∘ e.symm`.  That is where the
194	`≃` is used and cannot be weakened — for a non-invertible `K → K'` no such structure exists and
195	one must base-change `L` instead (`exists_witness_of_separable_extension`, a strictly harder
196	statement).
197	
198	The four instances about `L/K` are re-derived over `K'`: `Algebra K' L` and
199	`IsScalarTower k K' L` by `of_algebraMap_eq`, and `Module.Finite K' L`,
200	`Algebra.IsSeparable K' L` by mathlib's transports along the same commuting square
201	(`Module.Finite.of_equiv_equiv`, `Algebra.IsSeparable.of_equiv_equiv`).  The class equation is
202	`picEtAffineEquiv_naturality` plus `PicEtAff.map_mapAlg_eq_map`, and the witness clause `(W, hW,
203	hW1)` is carried through **untouched** — it lives over `L`, which did not move. -/
204	theorem isSplitWitness_map_overSpecMap {K K' : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K]
205	    [Field K'] [Algebra k K'] (e : K ≃ₐ[k] K') (nu : picEt C (overSpec k K))
206	    (h : IsSplitWitness C nu) :
207	    IsSplitWitness C (picEtMap C (Over.overSpecMap e.toAlgHom) nu) := by
208	  obtain ⟨L, hLfield, hkL, hKL, htow, hfin, hsep, M, hM, W, hW, hW1⟩ := h
209	  letI := hLfield
210	  letI := hkL
211	  letI := hKL
212	  haveI := htow
213	  haveI := hfin
214	  haveI := hsep
215	  -- the SAME `L`, now a `K'`-algebra along `e.symm`
216	  letI hK'L : Algebra K' L := ((algebraMap K L).comp e.symm.toRingHom).toAlgebra
217	  have halg : ∀ x : K, algebraMap K' L (e x) = algebraMap K L x := fun x => by
218	    change (algebraMap K L) (e.symm (e x)) = _
219	    rw [e.symm_apply_apply]
220	  haveI htow' : IsScalarTower k K' L := .of_algebraMap_eq fun x => by
221	    change algebraMap k L x = (algebraMap K L) (e.symm (algebraMap k K' x))
222	    rw [show e.symm (algebraMap k K' x) = algebraMap k K x from
223	      (e.symm.commutes x).trans rfl, ← IsScalarTower.algebraMap_apply k K L]
224	  -- the commuting square both mathlib transports are stated against
225	  have hcomp : ((algebraMap K' L).comp (e.toRingEquiv : K →+* K'))
226	      = ((RingEquiv.refl L : L →+* L)).comp (algebraMap K L) :=
227	    RingHom.ext fun x => halg x
228	  haveI hfin' : Module.Finite K' L :=
229	    Module.Finite.of_equiv_equiv e.toRingEquiv (RingEquiv.refl L) hcomp
230	  haveI hsep' : Algebra.IsSeparable K' L :=
231	    Algebra.IsSeparable.of_equiv_equiv e.toRingEquiv (RingEquiv.refl L) hcomp
232	  refine isSplitWitness_of_presenting_witness C _ M ?_ W hW hW1
233	  rw [picEtAffineEquiv_naturality, PicEtAff.map_mapAlg_eq_map e.toAlgHom halg]
234	  exact hM
235	
236	variable (C) in
237	/-- **Iso-invariance of `IsSplitWitness`, as an `iff`.**  The reverse direction is the forward
238	one at `e.symm`, since `overSpecMap` is functorial and `e.symm ∘ e = id`.  An `iff` is what the
239	locality assembly needs: a one-sided containment would not give openness. -/
240	theorem isSplitWitness_map_overSpecMap_iff {K K' : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K]
241	    [Field K'] [Algebra k K'] (e : K ≃ₐ[k] K') (nu : picEt C (overSpec k K)) :
242	    IsSplitWitness C (picEtMap C (Over.overSpecMap e.toAlgHom) nu)
243	      ↔ IsSplitWitness C nu := by
244	  refine ⟨fun h => ?_, isSplitWitness_map_overSpecMap C e nu⟩
245	  have hid : Over.overSpecMap (k := k) e.symm.toAlgHom ≫ Over.overSpecMap e.toAlgHom
246	      = 𝟙 (overSpec k K) := by
247	    rw [← Over.overSpecMap_comp, show e.symm.toAlgHom.comp e.toAlgHom = AlgHom.id k K from
248	      AlgHom.ext fun x => e.symm_apply_apply x, Over.overSpecMap_id]
249	  have hback := isSplitWitness_map_overSpecMap C e.symm _ h
250	  rwa [← picEtMap_comp, hid, picEtMap_id] at hback
251	
252	variable (C) in
253	/-- **`IsSplitWitnessIsoInvariant` — DISCHARGED.**
254	
255	The hypothesis `Picard/Pic0ChartLocusGeneralTest.lean` carries, and the only input standing
256	between the landed affine openness of `chartLocus` and CHART-U(b) at a general test.  With it,
257	`isOpen_chartLocus_of_affineLocal'` below is unconditional.
258	
259	The assembly is the naturality square in the slice (`Over.testPoint_comp`): reading the class at
260	`κ(t)` after restricting along `f` equals restricting along `Spec` of the residue-field
261	extension, which under the `IsIso` hypothesis is `Spec` of a `k`-algebra **equivalence** — and
262	along one of those `IsSplitWitness` is invariant. -/
263	theorem isSplitWitnessIsoInvariant_holds : IsSplitWitnessIsoInvariant C := by
264	  intro T T' f t hiso mu
265	  haveI := hiso
266	  have hfac : picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) (picEtMap C f mu)
267	      = picEtMap C (Over.overSpecMap (Over.testPointFieldAlgHom f t))
268	          (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint (T := T) (f.left.base t)) mu) := by
269	    rw [← picEtMap_comp, ← picEtMap_comp, Over.testPoint_comp f t]
270	  rw [hfac, show Over.testPointFieldAlgHom f t
271	      = (Over.testPointFieldAlgEquiv f t).toAlgHom from AlgHom.ext fun _ => rfl]
272	  exact isSplitWitness_map_overSpecMap_iff C (Over.testPointFieldAlgEquiv f t) _

281	    chartLocus C m Z (picEtMap C (Over.fromSpecAffine T U) lam)
282	      = (Over.fromSpecAffine T U).left.base ⁻¹' chartLocus C m Z lam :=
283	  chartLocus_fromSpecAffine_eq_preimage C (isSplitWitnessIsoInvariant_holds C) m Z T U lam

287	
288	If `chartLocus` is open over each affine-open test object of `T`, it is open over `T` — with no

292	    (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
293	    (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (lam : picEt C T)
294	    (haff : ∀ U : T.left.affineOpens,
295	      IsOpen (chartLocus C m Z (picEtMap C (Over.fromSpecAffine T U) lam))) :
296	    IsOpen (chartLocus C m Z lam) :=
297	  isOpen_chartLocus_of_affineLocal C (isSplitWitnessIsoInvariant_holds C) m Z T lam haff

11	/-!
12	# CHART-U(b)'s last residue: the descent direction `hconv`
13	
14	`Picard/Pic0ChartPresentationHalf.lean` splits `IsChartDatumPresentation` into a forward half
15	(proved there, by the trivial splitting) and a converse `hconv`, and its docstring prices the
16	converse as follows:
17	
18	> `hconv` is the descent direction: from a split witness over *some* extension `L_t/κ(t)`
19	> chosen per point, produce the datum's predicate at `κ(t)` itself.  Its two ingredients both
20	> exist — `hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_of_fieldExtension` carries a *datum* predicate across a
21	> field extension, and `hfib` identifies the classes — but composing them is not a rewrite,
22	> because the witness received lies in `μ`'s class at `L_t` rather than visibly in `D`'s at
23	> `κ(t)`.
24	
25	**That diagnosis is right, and it names two of the three ingredients.**  The missing one is
26	the reason the composition is not a rewrite: to see the received witness as lying in `D`'s
27	fibre class one must go *backwards* through `PicEtAff.unit`, and that step is
28	`PicEtAff.unit_injective` (`Picard/CechKernelLemma.lean:361`) — the unconditional close of the
29	ζ3 campaign, Kleiman 2.5(1).  With it the descent is three steps and no geometry:
30	
31	1. the split witness at `L_t` gives a presenting class `M` with
32	   `PicEtAff.map … (picEtAffineEquiv … μ_t) = PicEtAff.unit … (relPicMk … M)` and a witness
33	   divisor in `M` with vanishing `H¹`;
34	2. `hfib` at `t`, transported to `L_t`, says the *same* left-hand side equals
35	   `PicEtAff.unit … (relPicMk … (D's fibre class at L_t))`.  `unit_injective` then makes the
36	   two `relPicMk` arguments equal, and `relPicMk` is injective too — so `M` **is** `D`'s fibre
37	   class at `L_t`, which is what "visibly in `D`'s class" was missing;
38	3. hence `D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing L_t` holds by definition, and
39	   `hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_of_fieldExtension` brings it down to `κ(t)`.
40	
41	## What this file does and does not close
42	
43	It closes `hconv` **from a per-point transported `hfib`** — the statement
44	`IsChartDatumPlusFibreAt` below, which is `hfib`'s identity read at the chosen extension
45	rather than at `κ(t)`.  That is a real reduction: `hconv`'s conclusion is a statement about
46	witnesses and `H¹`, and what remains is a statement about *plus classes only*, with no witness,
47	no `H¹` and no divisor — exactly the shape §0.3's GAP-6 dictionary cannot see and the shape
48	`IsChartDatumPlusFibre` already has at `κ(t)`.
49	
50	**CORRECTION 2026-07-29 (r7), and this paragraph is why it is worth reading.**  The sentence that
51	stood here said the transport was not silently assumed because
52	`isChartDatumPlusFibreAt_of_isScalarTower` was "the honest statement" of it — and **that
53	declaration did not exist**, in this file or anywhere in the tree.  It was advertised by name and
54	never written (the failure mode `docstring-declaration-lists-unchecked`), and the effect was worse
55	than a dangling reference: the sentence made `hplus` read as bookkeeping already discharged, while
56	`hplus` was in fact the *whole* of B-4's remaining content.  The last clause — "so the composite
57	needs `hfib` at `κ(t)` and nothing else" — was therefore false of the theorem actually below it,
58	which takes `hplus` as a hypothesis.
59	
60	**It is true now, and of a different theorem.**  `Picard/Pic0ChartPlusFibreTower.lean` proves the
61	transport (three functoriality laws — `PicEtAff.map_map`, `PicEtAff.map_unit`, `relCurveMap_comp`
62	— and no geometry) and derives `IsChartDatumPresentation` from `hfib` alone as
63	`isChartDatumPresentation_of_plusFibre_tower`.  **Prefer that theorem**; the one below remains
64	correct and is the general form.
65	
66	**One further finding, about the statement of `hasWitnessH1Vanishing_of_isSplitWitness_at` below
67	rather than its proof.**  Its `hplus` binder quantifies `(_ : Algebra A L)` universally with only
68	the `k`-tower imposed, and that is strictly stronger than the proof consumes: the proof takes the
69	`A`-structure from its own `htow` and uses `hplus` at *that* instance only.  The extra strength is
70	not harmless — `IsChartDatumPlusFibreAt` mentions `relCurveMap C A L`, so at an `Algebra A L`
71	unrelated to the composite `A → κ(t) → L` the right-hand side pulls `D.cechPicClass` along a
72	different morphism and `hfib` cannot imply it.  So the `∀`-form is not merely hard to supply, it
73	is the wrong statement.  `hasWitnessH1Vanishing_of_isSplitWitness_tower` (same file as the
74	transport) is this theorem with `IsScalarTower A κ(t) L` added to that binder — the third
75	component `towerOfResidueFieldExtension` already returns, and which the proof below already
76	destructures and then discards.
77	
78	## Main declarations
79	
80	* `AlgebraicGeometry.IsChartDatumPlusFibreAt` — the plus-class identity at a *given*
81	  extension of the residue field.  Witness-free.
82	* `AlgebraicGeometry.hasWitnessH1Vanishing_of_isSplitWitness_at` — **the descent step**: a
83	  split witness whose splitting field satisfies that identity gives the datum's predicate
84	  there, hence (by the field-extension `iff`) at `κ(t)`.  This is where
85	  `PicEtAff.unit_injective` is spent.
86	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isChartDatumPresentation_of_plusFibre` — **CHART-U(b)'s residue closed
87	  modulo the plus-class identity**: `IsChartDatumPresentation` from `hfib` at `κ(t)` together
88	  with the per-point transported identity, with no separate `hconv`.
89	-/
