115	/-! ## The plus-class identity at a chosen extension -/
116	
117	variable (C π) in
118	/-- **The plus-class identity of `IsChartDatumPlusFibre`, read at a given extension `L` of the
119	residue field** rather than at `κ(t)` itself.
120	
121	Witness-free, `H¹`-free and divisor-free, exactly like `IsChartDatumPlusFibre`: it says the
122	plus class obtained by restricting `μ` to `κ(t)` and then reading it over `L` is the plus-unit
123	of `D`'s fibre class at `L`.
124	
125	This is the form the descent step below consumes, because a split witness for `μ` at `t`
126	produces its data over an extension it chooses, not over `κ(t)`. -/
127	def IsChartDatumPlusFibreAt {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
128	    (μ : picEt C (overSpec k A)) (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C A π)
129	    (t : (overSpec k A).left) (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L]
130	    [Algebra (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) L]
131	    [IsScalarTower k (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) L] [Algebra A L]
132	    [IsScalarTower k A L] : Prop :=
133	  PicEtAff.map C L
134	      (picEtAffineEquiv C (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t)
135	        (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) μ))
136	    = PicEtAff.unit C L
137	        (relPicMk C (overSpec k L)
138	          (Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C A L) D.cechPicClass))
139	
140	/-! ## The descent step -/
141	
142	variable (C π) in
143	/-- **THE DESCENT STEP** — `hconv` at one point, given the plus-class identity at the
144	splitting field.
145	
146	A split witness for `μ`'s fibre at `t` hands over a finite separable `L/κ(t)`, a presenting
147	class `M` over `L`, and a divisor `W` in `M` with vanishing `H¹`.  The plus-class identity at
148	`L` says the *same* left-hand side that `M` presents is the plus-unit of `D`'s fibre class at
149	`L`.  So:
150	
151	* `PicEtAff.unit_injective` (`Picard/CechKernelLemma.lean:361`, Kleiman 2.5(1) — the
152	  unconditional close of the ζ3 campaign) makes the two `relPicMk` arguments equal;
153	* `relPicMk` is injective (`relPicMk_injective_of_subsingleton`), so `M` **is** `D`'s fibre
154	  class at `L`;
155	* `W` therefore witnesses `D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing L` by definition, and
156	  `hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_of_fieldExtension` carries that down to `κ(t)`.
157	
158	**This is the ingredient `Pic0ChartPresentationHalf`'s docstring was missing.**  It diagnosed
159	correctly that "the witness received lies in `μ`'s class at `L_t` rather than visibly in `D`'s
160	at `κ(t)`", and named the two transport lemmas — but the step that makes the class *visible*
161	is not a transport at all: it is the injectivity of the plus unit, which the tree has had since
162	the ζ3 close and which no CHART-U row cites. -/
163	theorem hasWitnessH1Vanishing_of_isSplitWitness_at {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
164	    (μ : picEt C (overSpec k A)) (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C A π)
165	    (t : (overSpec k A).left)
166	    (hplus : ∀ (L : Type u) (_ : Field L) (_ : Algebra k L)
167	      (_ : Algebra (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) L)
168	      (_ : IsScalarTower k (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) L)
169	      (_ : Algebra A L) (_ : IsScalarTower k A L),
170	      IsChartDatumPlusFibreAt C π μ D t L)
171	    (htow : ∀ (L : Type u) (_ : Field L) (_ : Algebra k L)
172	      (_ : Algebra (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) L)
173	      (_ : IsScalarTower k (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) L),
174	      Σ' (_ : Algebra A L) (_ : IsScalarTower k A L),
175	        IsScalarTower A (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) L)
176	    (h : IsSplitWitness C (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) μ)) :
177	    D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) := by
178	  obtain ⟨L, hLf, hLk, hLK, hLtow, hLfin, hLsep, M, hM, W, hW, hW1⟩ := h
179	  obtain ⟨hAL, hAtow, hATow⟩ := htow L hLf hLk hLK hLtow
180	  -- the plus-class identity at `L`, and the presenting identity the witness came with
181	  have hid : PicEtAff.unit C L (relPicMk C (overSpec k L) M)
182	      = PicEtAff.unit C L
183	        (relPicMk C (overSpec k L)
184	          (Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C A L) D.cechPicClass)) := by
185	    rw [← hM]
186	    exact hplus L hLf hLk hLK hLtow hAL hAtow
187	  -- `unit_injective` then `relPicMk` injective: `M` IS `D`'s fibre class at `L`
188	  have hMcl : M = Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C A L) D.cechPicClass :=
189	    relPicMk_injective_of_subsingleton C (overSpec k L)
190	      (PicEtAff.unit_injective C L hid)
191	  -- so `W` witnesses `D`'s predicate at `L`, and the field-extension `iff` descends it
192	  refine (D.hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_of_fieldExtension
193	    (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) L).mpr ⟨W, ?_, hW1⟩
194	  rw [hW, hMcl]
195	
196	/-! ## The `htow` hypothesis is satisfiable, checked rather than assumed
197	
198	`htow` returns *data* (three instances), so it could in principle be an unmeetable demand and
199	the descent step vacuous — the failure mode memory `isolating-a-residue-as-a-class` records
200	from the other direction.  It is not: the composite tower always exists. -/
201	
202	/-- **`htow` is constructible**, at any `L` over the residue field.
203	
204	The `A`-algebra structure on `L` is the composite `A → κ(t) → L`, where `A → κ(t)` is the
205	tree's own `Over.instAlgebraTestPointFieldAffine`.  Both towers then hold by
206	`IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq`.
207	
208	Worth stating rather than inlining, because `Algebra A L` does **not** synthesize from the
209	hypotheses of `hasWitnessH1Vanishing_of_isSplitWitness_at` — measured — so a reader would
210	otherwise have to guess whether `htow` is a genuine obligation or bookkeeping.  It is
211	bookkeeping, and this is the proof. -/
212	def towerOfResidueFieldExtension {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
213	    (t : (overSpec k A).left) (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L]
214	    [Algebra (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) L]
215	    [IsScalarTower k (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) L] :
216	    Σ' (_ : Algebra A L) (_ : IsScalarTower k A L),
217	      IsScalarTower A (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) L := by
218	  letI : Algebra A L :=
219	    ((algebraMap (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) L).comp
220	      (algebraMap A (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t))).toAlgebra
221	  haveI htow : IsScalarTower A (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) L :=
222	    IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq fun _ => rfl
223	  refine ⟨_, IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq fun x => ?_, htow⟩
224	  change (algebraMap k L) x
225	      = (algebraMap (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) L)
226	          ((algebraMap A (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t)) ((algebraMap k A) x))
227	  rw [← IsScalarTower.algebraMap_apply k A (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t),
228	    ← IsScalarTower.algebraMap_apply k (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) L]
229	
230	/-- **`IsChartDatumPlusFibreAt` at `L := κ(t)` IS `IsChartDatumPlusFibre` at `t`** — by
231	`Iff.rfl`, so the generalisation in `L` is a genuine generalisation of the *same* equation and
232	not a different statement that happens to specialise.
233	
234	This is the upper half of the two-sided check on `hplus` below, and it is the sharp one: it shows
235	the extra strength of `hplus` over `hfib` is exactly "the same identity at every extension", so a
236	lane reading `hplus` knows precisely what it owes beyond `hfib` — the naturality of `cechPicClass`
237	along `κ(t) → L`, and nothing else.
238	
239	**The lower half was measured too, and is recorded here because it cannot be a theorem.**  A
240	reduction whose new hypothesis is *satisfiable by construction* is vacuous, and `D` in
241	`IsChartDatumPlusFibreAt` is chosen by the consumer — exactly the configuration in which that
242	happens.  Probed at arbitrary `μ`, `D`, `t`, `L`: `rfl` fails on the left-hand side, and `simp`
243	and `aesop` both leave unsolved goals.  So it is a genuine equation between two plus classes and
244	not a `Prop` true for free.  (A passing automation attempt would have refuted the reduction, which
245	is why the probe is worth running before pricing anything as a residue.)
246	
247	**And the probe has a second form, which the first does not cover.**  Junk-inhabitation is the risk
248	when the hypothesis is *consumer-chosen* — `D` here.  When it is *determined* by the setting, the
249	mirror risk is **unsatisfiability**: a reduction to a false hypothesis passes every `sorry` census
250	and every axiom probe, because it then *is* a theorem.  `hplus` is determined in `μ`, so that
251	direction needs a witness, and the witness is landed and unconditional:
252	`exists_splitting_of_picEt` produces, for **any** plus class over **any** reading field, a finite
253	separable `L` and a presenting class `M` with exactly the identity `hplus` asserts.  So the
254	plus-class identity is *inhabited* at every `μ`, not merely consistent. -/
255	theorem isChartDatumPlusFibreAt_self {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
256	    (μ : picEt C (overSpec k A)) (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C A π)
257	    (t : (overSpec k A).left) (h : IsChartDatumPlusFibre C π μ D) :
258	    IsChartDatumPlusFibreAt C π μ D t (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) :=
259	  h t
260	
261	/-! ## CHART-U(b)'s residue, assembled -/
262	
263	variable (C π) in
264	/-- **`IsChartDatumPresentation` WITH NO SEPARATE `hconv`** — CHART-U(b)'s residue reduced to a
265	witness-free statement about plus classes.
266	
267	`isChartDatumPresentation_of_plusFibre_of_converse` asks for `hfib` *and* `hconv`.  This asks
268	for `hfib` and the per-point plus-class identity at the splitting field, which is `hfib`'s own
269	statement read at `L` instead of at `κ(t)` — and discharges `hconv` from it via the descent step
270	above.  `htow` is supplied by `towerOfResidueFieldExtension`, so it is not an
271	obligation on the caller.
272	
273	**What this buys the CHART-U(b) row.**  Its residue was "the pointwise presentation", an `↔`
274	one half of which involved witnesses and `H¹`.  Both halves are now witness-free: the forward
275	one was already (`isSplitWitness_of_hasWitnessH1Vanishing`, by the trivial splitting) and the
276	converse is now, by the plus-unit injectivity.  So the whole of CHART-U(b) reduces to
277	`cechPicClass` base-change identities — which is what the row's own §0.3 retraction predicted
278	("a `cechPicClass` base-change statement, and not any construction") and what
279	`Pic0ChartLocusIsOpen`'s header calls the residue.
280	
281	**What it does not buy — SUPERSEDED 2026-07-29 (r7).**  This paragraph said the remaining identity
282	is at *every* extension `L` of `κ(t)`, strictly more than `IsChartDatumPlusFibre` asks, and that
283	whether the two are equivalent "is the naturality of `cechPicClass` under `κ(t) → L`, which this
284	file does not settle".  **They are equivalent, and the answer was cheaper than the framing
285	suggested**: the identity at `L` is the identity at `κ(t)` pushed forward along `PicEtAff.map C L`,
286	so it needs `PicEtAff.map_map`, `PicEtAff.map_unit` and `relCurveMap_comp` and nothing about
287	`cechPicClass` specifically.  `isChartDatumPlusFibreAt_of_isScalarTower`
288	(`Picard/Pic0ChartPlusFibreTower.lean`) is the transport, and
289	`isChartDatumPresentation_of_plusFibre_tower` is this theorem with the `hplus` argument
290	removed.  Use that one.
291	
292	The one caveat the transport does carry is the tower compatibility `IsScalarTower A κ(t) L`, which
293	is genuinely needed (see the correction in this file's header) and is supplied by
294	`towerOfResidueFieldExtension` — so it is not an obligation on any caller. -/
295	theorem isChartDatumPresentation_of_plusFibre {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
296	    {μ : picEt C (overSpec k A)} {D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C A π}
297	    (hfib : IsChartDatumPlusFibre C π μ D)
298	    (hplus : ∀ (t : (overSpec k A).left) (L : Type u) (_ : Field L) (_ : Algebra k L)
299	      (_ : Algebra (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) L)
300	      (_ : IsScalarTower k (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) L)
301	      (_ : Algebra A L) (_ : IsScalarTower k A L),
302	      IsChartDatumPlusFibreAt C π μ D t L) :
303	    IsChartDatumPresentation C π μ D :=

11

14	
15	* `D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing κ(t)` — the datum's fibre predicate, and
16	* `IsSplitWitness C (fibre of μ at κ(t))` — the split predicate `chartLocus` is defined by.

18	That file's header prices it as a *construction* rather than bookkeeping, and is right to: the
19	splitting field `L` in `IsSplitWitness` is quantified **per point**, so no single datum obviously
20	matches it everywhere.
21	
22	**This file discharges the `→` direction from a hypothesis that mentions no witness at all.**
23	
24	## What makes the forward direction cheap now
25	
26	The datum side hands you a witness divisor `W` over `κ(t)` in the class
27	`CechPic.map (relCurveMap C A κ(t)) D.cechPicClass`, with vanishing `H¹`.  To build
28	`IsSplitWitness` you must exhibit a finite separable extension over which the *fibre of `μ`* is
29	honest, with a witness in its class.  Take the extension to be `κ(t)` itself — the identity
30	extension, finite and separable — and the witness to be `W`.
31	
32	That is exactly `isSplitWitness_of_presenting_witness_self`
33	(`Picard/Pic0ChartTwistSplit.lean`), the trivial splitting `L := K`.  Memory item I-0564 had
34	recorded that instance as **unelaborable** and singled it out as "worth wanting"; it is a
35	one-liner once the existentials are staged rather than bundled, and this file is the first
36	consumer that needed it.

39	that the datum's fibre class, read as a plus class, *is* the fibre of `μ`.  That is
40	`IsChartDatumPlusFibre` below — a naturality identity between `PicEtAff.map ∘ picEtAffineEquiv`

8	/-!
9	# THE PRODUCER: `IsChartDatumPlusFibre` for a class in the image of the sheafification unit
10	
11	## What this file closes
12	
13	`Picard/Pic0ChartLocusPlusFibre.lean` proves CHART-U(b) at a general test from a per-affine-piece
14	`IsChartDatumPlusFibre`, and its header says plainly what it does not do:
15	
16	> The hypothesis is a *per-affine-piece existence of a datum with the plus-class property*, and
17	> nothing here produces such a datum.
18	
19	**This file produces one**, and the ingredient that was missing is smaller than four successive
20	sessions on this leaf priced it: on an **affine** test the canonical field point `Over.testPoint t`
21	**is** the base-change morphism `overSpecMap A κ(t)`.  Both sides are `Spec` of the same ring map —
22	`Over.instAlgebraTestPointFieldAffine` is *defined* as `Spec.preimage` of `fromSpecResidueField`,
23	so `Spec.map_preimage` closes it — but nothing in the tree said so, and every plus-class identity
24	on this lane is an identity between a class pulled along `Over.testPoint` and one pulled along
25	`relCurveMap`.  Without the comparison the two sides are not even syntactically comparable; with
26	it they are the same class.
27	
28	## The shape of the producer, and its one genuine restriction
29	
30	`IsChartDatumPlusFibre C π μ D` compares `μ`'s fibre at `κ(t)`, read as a plus class, with the
31	plus-*unit* of `D`'s fibre class.  So the natural hypothesis on `μ` is that it is *already* a
32	plus unit — i.e. in the image of the sheafification unit `relPicToPicEt` — and then `D` comes
33	from `exists_cechPicClass_eq` applied to any Čech representative.
34	
35	That restriction is real and is named `IsPlusHonest` below.  It is **not** vacuous and **not**
36	automatic:
37	
38	* not automatic — a general plus class over `Spec A` is `PicEtAff.mk E x` for an étale cover `E`,
39	  and `Picard/Pic0ChartHonest.lean` is precisely the record that it becomes honest only over
40	  `E.Carrier`, not over `A`.  So `IsPlusHonest` is a genuine hypothesis, not a restatement;
41	* not vacuous, and this is the payoff — the range of `relPicToPicEt` is a **subgroup**, and every
42	  class the chart layer twists by is in it: the θ-family (`thetaFamily_isPlusHonest`), the
43	  Σ-family, and the Abel value itself (`abelDiv_isPlusHonest`).  So `chartTwist` preserves
44	  honesty, and CHART-U(b) becomes **unconditional** on exactly the classes DAT-C's Σ-chart reads.
45	
46	  **A CORRECTION TO THIS PARAGRAPH, from a fresh-context review of the commit that first wrote
47	  it, and it is the same failure this leaf recorded one round earlier.**  When first committed the
48	  sentence above cited `abelDiv_isPlusHonest` **and that declaration did not exist** — a
49	  workspace-wide grep returned exactly one hit, the sentence itself.  That is precisely the
50	  failure mode r7 diagnosed (`docstring-declaration-lists-unchecked`) and filed a lesson about,
51	  reproduced by the very session that filed it, inside its own *non-vacuity* argument.
52	  A kernel check, a `sorry` census and an axiom probe are all silent about it.
53	
54	  It also mattered mathematically, which is why it was worth writing rather than deleting: the
55	  θ- and Σ-witnesses are the **twist factors**, which `chartTwist_isPlusHonest` discharges anyway,
56	  so they say nothing about the class being *charted*.  Since `chartValue = abelDiv · Σ · (θᵐ)⁻¹`,
57	  honesty of a chart value reduces to honesty of `abelDiv` alone — so `abelDiv_isPlusHonest` was
58	  carrying the whole of the final clause.  It is now proved (below), so the paragraph stands as
59	  written; had it not been, the honest statement would have been "no residue beyond
60	  `IsPlusHonest lam`", with the Σ-chart clause unproved.
61	
62	## Main declarations
63	
64	* `AlgebraicGeometry.testPoint_eq_overSpecMap` — **the comparison**: on an affine test the
65	  canonical field point is the base-change morphism.
66	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isChartDatumPlusFibre_of_relPicToPicEt` — the producer, with the datum given.
67	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isChartDatumPlusFibre_of_mem_range` — **the producer proper**: for a
68	  class in the image of the unit, a datum with the plus-class property EXISTS.
69	* `AlgebraicGeometry.IsPlusHonest` — the per-affine-piece form, closed under the group operations.
70	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isOpen_chartLocus_of_isPlusHonest` — **CHART-U(b) with no residue** for an
71	  honest class, and `chartLocusOpensOfIsPlusHonest` the same open as DATA.
72	-/

185	    (C := C) (B := A) (π := π) L₀
186	  exact ⟨D, isChartDatumPlusFibre_of_relPicToPicEt C π L₀ D hD⟩

190	variable (C) in
191	/-- **The honesty hypothesis: `μ` is a plus unit on every affine piece of the test.**
192	
193	This is the one thing the producer needs of `μ`, and it is a genuine hypothesis rather than a
194	restatement: a plus class over `Spec A` is `PicEtAff.mk E x` for an étale cover `E`, and
195	`Picard/Pic0ChartHonest.lean` is the record that it becomes honest over `E.Carrier` and not over
196	`A`.  So `IsPlusHonest` is exactly the gap between an arbitrary class and one the producer reaches.

198	It is stated per affine piece because that is the shape `isOpen_chartLocus_of_plusFibre` consumes;
199	over an affine test it is the single condition that `μ` is in the range of `relPicToPicEt`. -/
200	def IsPlusHonest (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (μ : picEt C T) : Prop :=
201	  ∀ U : T.left.affineOpens, ∃ z : relPic C (overSpec k Γ(T.left, U.1)),
202	    relPicToPicEt C (overSpec k Γ(T.left, U.1)) z
203	      = picEtMap C (Over.fromSpecAffine T U) μ

210	    (hμ : IsPlusHonest C T μ) (hν : IsPlusHonest C T ν) :
211	    IsPlusHonest C T (μ * ν) := by
212	  intro U
213	  obtain ⟨z, hz⟩ := hμ U
214	  obtain ⟨w, hw⟩ := hν U
215	  exact ⟨z * w, by rw [map_mul, hz, hw, map_mul]⟩

222	    IsPlusHonest C T μ⁻¹ := by
223	  intro U
224	  obtain ⟨z, hz⟩ := hμ U

245	theorem thetaFamily_isPlusHonest (L₀ : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CechPic)

247	    IsPlusHonest C T (thetaFamily C L₀ T) := by
248	  intro U
249	  refine ⟨relPicAlgMap C (Algebra.ofId k Γ(T.left, U.1)) (relPicMk C (overSpec k k) L₀), ?_⟩
250	  rw [thetaFamily_natural]
251	  exact (picEtAffineEquiv C Γ(T.left, U.1)).injective (by
252	    rw [picEtAffineEquiv_relPicToPicEt, thetaFamily_overSpec_affineEquiv])

258	    IsPlusHonest C T (sigmaFamily C Z T) :=

263	file's header cited by name before it existed (see the header's own retraction).

265	The θ- and Σ-family witnesses above are the *twist factors*, which `chartTwist_isPlusHonest`

271	It is cheap for a structural reason: `abelDiv`'s components are `abelDivPlus`, i.e. `PicEtAff.unit`

273	`relPicMap` — so the witness on the piece `U` is the class of the *restricted* family, and
274	`abelDiv_val` plus `picEtMap_abelDiv` line the two up. -/
275	theorem abelDiv_isPlusHonest {n : ℕ} (T : Over (Spec (.of k)))
276	    (s : divFamZar C π n T) :
277	    IsPlusHonest C T (abelDiv C π n T s) := by
278	  intro U
279	  refine ⟨relPicMk C (overSpec k Γ(T.left, U.1))
280	    ((divFamZarAffineEquiv C π n Γ(T.left, U.1)
281	      (divFamZar.map C π n (Over.fromSpecAffine T U) s)).picClass), ?_⟩
282	  rw [picEtMap_abelDiv, abelDiv_overSpec]
283	  rfl

286	/-- **`chartTwist` PRESERVES honesty** — the reason the producer reaches the Σ-chart.
287	
288	`chartTwist λ = λ · θᵐ · Σ⁻¹`, and both twist factors are θ-families, hence honest at every test
289	with no hypothesis.  Since honesty is a subgroup condition, the twisted class is honest exactly
290	when `λ` is.
291	
292	So the residue of CHART-U(b) is **the λ-factor alone**: no twist bookkeeping enters, which is the
293	mis-pricing the §3.3 correction 5 records. -/
294	theorem chartTwist_isPlusHonest (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
295	    (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) {lam : picEt C T} (hlam : IsPlusHonest C T lam) :
296	    IsPlusHonest C T (chartTwist C m Z T lam) := by
297	  rw [chartTwist]
298	  exact (hlam.mul C ((thetaFamily_isPlusHonest C (thetaCechClass C) T).pow C m)).mul C
299	    ((sigmaFamily_isPlusHonest C Z T).inv C)

302	
303	set_option linter.overlappingInstances false in
304	variable (C π) in
305	/-- **CHART-U(b) AT A GENERAL TEST, WITH NO RESIDUE**, for a class that is honest on the affine
306	pieces of the test.
307	
308	`isOpen_chartLocus_of_plusFibre` needs a per-piece datum with the plus-class property;
309	`exists_isChartDatumPlusFibre_of_mem_range` produces one from honesty, and
310	`chartTwist_isPlusHonest` says the twist does not disturb honesty.  So the whole chain — the
311	engine, RE-5, the dictionary, the fibre-field invariance, `haff`, the presentation, `hconv`,
312	`hplus`, and now the producer — closes on the single hypothesis `IsPlusHonest`.
313	
314	`IsAffineHom π` follows from `IsFinite π`, whence the disabled overlapping-instance linter — the
315	same configuration `chartLocusAffineLocal_of_plusFibre` carries and for the same reason. -/
316	theorem isOpen_chartLocus_of_isPlusHonest
317	    (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom)
318	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
319	    (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (lam : picEt C T) (hlam : IsPlusHonest C T lam) :

321	  isOpen_chartLocus_of_plusFibre C π hπ m Z T lam fun U =>
322	    exists_isChartDatumPlusFibre_of_mem_range C π _
323	      (by
324	        obtain ⟨z, hz⟩ := chartTwist_isPlusHonest C m Z T hlam U
325	        exact ⟨z, hz.trans (picEtMap_chartTwist m Z (Over.fromSpecAffine T U) lam)⟩)

327	set_option linter.overlappingInstances false in

334	def chartLocusOpensOfIsPlusHonest
335	    (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom)
336	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
337	    (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (lam : picEt C T) (hlam : IsPlusHonest C T lam) :
338	    T.left.Opens where
339	  carrier := chartLocus C m Z lam
340	  is_open' := isOpen_chartLocus_of_isPlusHonest C π hπ m Z T lam hlam

343	lemma mem_chartLocusOpensOfIsPlusHonest
344	    {hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom}
345	    {m : ℕ} {Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor}

9	/-!
10	# `hplus` from `hfib`: the tower transport CHART-U(b) was still owed
11	
12	## What this file closes, and why it was not already closed
13	
14	`Picard/Pic0ChartPresentationConverse.lean` reduces CHART-U(b)'s residue
15	`IsChartDatumPresentation` to `hfib` (`IsChartDatumPlusFibre`, the plus-class identity at each
16	residue field `κ(t)`) **plus** `hplus` — the same identity read at an arbitrary extension
17	`L/κ(t)` (`IsChartDatumPlusFibreAt`).  Its own docstring names the missing link:
18	
19	> It does **not** silently assume the transport: `isChartDatumPlusFibreAt_of_isScalarTower` is
20	> the honest statement of when the `κ(t)`-level `hfib` gives the `L_t`-level one, and its
21	> hypothesis is a tower compatibility that the split witness's own instances supply.
22	
23	**`isChartDatumPlusFibreAt_of_isScalarTower` does not exist.**  It is named in that paragraph and
24	nowhere else in the tree — a declaration advertised by a docstring and never written, the failure
25	mode memory `docstring-declaration-lists-unchecked` records.  The consequence was not cosmetic:
26	the sentence made `hplus` look like bookkeeping already discharged, while `hplus` was in fact the
27	*whole* of B-4's remaining content.  That reading is what this file removes, by proving the
28	transport rather than citing it.
29	
30	## The mathematics, and why it is a transport and not a base-change theorem
31	
32	`hplus` at `L` asks for
33	
34	  `PicEtAff.map C L (picEtAffineEquiv C κ(t) μ_t) = PicEtAff.unit C L (relPicMk C L (D_L))`
35	
36	where `D_L` is `D.cechPicClass` pulled to `L`, and `hfib` at `t` gives exactly that identity with
37	`L` replaced by `κ(t)`.  So apply the restriction homomorphism `PicEtAff.map C L` to `hfib t` and
38	identify both sides:
39	
40	* **Left.** `PicEtAff.map_map` over the tower `κ(t) → L`: restricting twice is restricting once,
41	  so `map C L (map C κ(t) x) = map C L x`.  The `κ(t)`-level `map` in `hfib` is `map C κ(t)`
42	  applied to the fibre, which `map_id` collapses — this is where the two spellings meet.
43	* **Right.** `PicEtAff.map_unit`, the naturality of the plus unit: the image of a unit is the unit
44	  of the transported `relPic` class.  Then `relPicAlgMap_mk` turns `relPicMap` of a `relPicMk`
45	  into `relPicMk` of a `CechPic.map`, and `relCurveMap_comp` — the *composition* law of the
46	  relative-curve comparisons over `k → A → κ(t) → L`, already landed in `DivisorFamilyMapAlg` for
47	  the divisor functor laws — identifies the two-step pull `A → κ(t) → L` with the one-step pull
48	  `A → L` that `IsChartDatumPlusFibreAt` names.
49	
50	So the transport is three functoriality laws and no geometry.  All three were in the tree; what
51	was missing is that nobody had put them together, because the docstring said somebody had.
52	
53	## The tower hypothesis is real, and it is `IsScalarTower A κ(t) L`
54	
55	The one thing the transport genuinely needs beyond instances already in scope is that the
56	`A`-algebra structure on `L` agrees with the composite `A → κ(t) → L`.  It is not automatic:
57	`IsChartDatumPlusFibreAt` takes `[Algebra A L]` as a *separate* instance from
58	`[Algebra κ(t) L]`, so a caller could in principle supply an unrelated one, and then the
59	right-hand sides genuinely differ (the `CechPic` class pulled along `A → L` is not the one
60	pulled along `A → κ(t) → L`).  Naming it as a hypothesis is therefore the honest statement, and
61	it is exactly the third component `towerOfResidueFieldExtension` already produces — so the
62	composite below needs nothing from the caller that the descent step did not already have.
63	
64	## Main declarations
65	
66	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isChartDatumPlusFibreAt_of_isScalarTower` — **the transport**, under the
67	  tower compatibility: `hfib` at `κ(t)` gives `hplus` at any `L`.  The declaration the converse
68	  file's docstring advertised.
69	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isChartDatumPresentation_of_plusFibre_tower` — **CHART-U(b)'s residue from
70	  `hfib` ALONE**, with no `hplus` side condition: the transport supplies it at every point and
71	  every extension, and `towerOfResidueFieldExtension` supplies the tower.
72	-/

100	variable (C π) in
101	/-- **THE TRANSPORT** — `hplus` at an arbitrary extension `L` from `hfib` at `κ(t)`.
102	
103	This is the declaration `Pic0ChartPresentationConverse`'s header advertises by name and which did
104	not exist.  Under the tower compatibility `IsScalarTower A κ(t) L` — the one thing that is *not*
105	automatic, and the third component `towerOfResidueFieldExtension` already returns — the plus-class
106	identity at `κ(t)` implies the same identity at `L`.
107	
108	Proof: apply `PicEtAff.map C L` to `hfib t`.  `PicEtAff.map_map` collapses the two-step
109	restriction on the left; `PicEtAff.map_unit` moves it through the unit on the right; and
110	`relCurveMap_comp` over `A → κ(t) → L` identifies the two-step pull of `D.cechPicClass` with the
111	one-step pull `IsChartDatumPlusFibreAt` names.  Three functoriality laws, no geometry. -/
112	theorem isChartDatumPlusFibreAt_of_isScalarTower {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
113	    (μ : picEt C (overSpec k A)) (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C A π)
114	    (t : (overSpec k A).left) (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L]
115	    [Algebra (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) L]
116	    [IsScalarTower k (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) L] [Algebra A L]
117	    [IsScalarTower k A L]
118	    [IsScalarTower A (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) L]
119	    (hfib : IsChartDatumPlusFibre C π μ D) :

123	  refine h.trans (congrArg (PicEtAff.unit C L) (congrArg (relPicMk C (overSpec k L)) ?_))
124	  -- the two-step pull `A → κ(t) → L` is the one-step pull `A → L`.  Rewriting the RHS's
125	  -- morphism into the composite keeps the `CechPic` type index fixed, which is what makes
126	  -- this a legal `rw` where rewriting the LHS is not (the two spellings `relCurve C κ(t)`
127	  -- and `(C ⊗ overSpec k κ(t)).left` are `rfl`-equal but block the motive).
128	  rw [← relCurveMap_comp (C := C) (R := A)
129	      (R' := Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) (R'' := L),

133	/-! ## The descent step with the tower restricted
134	
135	The transport above cannot be fed to `hasWitnessH1Vanishing_of_isSplitWitness_at` as it stands,
136	and the reason is a genuine finding about that theorem's statement rather than a typing nuisance.
137	Its `hplus` binder reads
138	
139	  `∀ (L) … (_ : Algebra A L) (_ : IsScalarTower k A L), IsChartDatumPlusFibreAt C π μ D t L`
140	
141	— universally quantified over the `A`-algebra structure on `L`, with only the `k`-tower imposed.
142	That is **strictly stronger than the theorem consumes**: its proof obtains the `A`-structure from
143	its own `htow` argument and uses `hplus` at *that* instance only.  And the extra strength is not
144	harmless, because `IsChartDatumPlusFibreAt` mentions `relCurveMap C A L`, which depends on the
145	`A`-algebra structure: for an `Algebra A L` unrelated to the composite `A → κ(t) → L`, the
146	right-hand side pulls `D.cechPicClass` along a different morphism and the identity has no reason
147	to hold.  So the `∀`-form is not merely unprovable from `hfib` — it is the wrong statement, and
148	`hfib` cannot imply it.
149	
150	This is the failure mode `price-the-instances-not-the-data` names, occurring inside a binder: the
151	hypothesis quantifies instances, and quantifying one instance too freely turns a provable
152	obligation into an unprovable one.  So the step is restated below with the tower compatibility
153	`IsScalarTower A κ(t) L` in the binder — exactly the third component
154	`towerOfResidueFieldExtension` already returns and which the landed step already destructures and
155	then discards.  The proof is the landed one; only the binder changes. -/
156	
157	variable (C π) in
158	/-- **The descent step, with the `A`-tower in `hplus`'s binder** — otherwise
159	`hasWitnessH1Vanishing_of_isSplitWitness_at` verbatim.
160	
161	The landed form asks for the plus-class identity at *every* `A`-algebra structure on `L`; this
162	asks for it only at those compatible with `A → κ(t) → L`, which is all its proof ever uses and
163	all that `hfib` can give (see the section note above).  With this binder the transport
164	`isChartDatumPlusFibreAt_of_isScalarTower` applies, and CHART-U(b)'s residue follows from `hfib`
165	alone. -/
166	theorem hasWitnessH1Vanishing_of_isSplitWitness_tower {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
167	    (μ : picEt C (overSpec k A)) (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C A π)
168	    (t : (overSpec k A).left)
169	    (hplus : ∀ (L : Type u) (_ : Field L) (_ : Algebra k L)
170	      (_ : Algebra (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) L)
171	      (_ : IsScalarTower k (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) L)
172	      (_ : Algebra A L) (_ : IsScalarTower k A L)
173	      (_ : IsScalarTower A (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) L),
174	      IsChartDatumPlusFibreAt C π μ D t L)
175	    (h : IsSplitWitness C (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) μ)) :
176	    D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) := by
177	  obtain ⟨L, hLf, hLk, hLK, hLtow, hLfin, hLsep, M, hM, W, hW, hW1⟩ := h
178	  obtain ⟨hAL, hAtow, hATow⟩ := towerOfResidueFieldExtension (k := k) t L
179	  have hid : PicEtAff.unit C L (relPicMk C (overSpec k L) M)
180	      = PicEtAff.unit C L
181	        (relPicMk C (overSpec k L)
182	          (Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C A L) D.cechPicClass)) := by
183	    rw [← hM]
184	    exact hplus L hLf hLk hLK hLtow hAL hAtow hATow
185	  have hMcl : M = Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C A L) D.cechPicClass :=
186	    relPicMk_injective_of_subsingleton C (overSpec k L)
187	      (PicEtAff.unit_injective C L hid)
188	  refine (D.hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_of_fieldExtension
189	    (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) L).mpr ⟨W, ?_, hW1⟩
190	  rw [hW, hMcl]
191	
192	/-! ## CHART-U(b)'s residue from `hfib` alone -/
193	
194	variable (C π) in
195	/-- **`IsChartDatumPresentation` FROM `hfib` ALONE** — no `hplus` side condition.
196	
197	`isChartDatumPresentation_of_plusFibre` asks for `hfib` *and* the per-point identity at every
198	extension.  The transport above supplies the second from the first, and
199	`towerOfResidueFieldExtension` supplies the tower instance the transport needs, so the caller
200	owes only `hfib`.
201	
202	**What this settles about the CHART-U(b) row.**  The row's state as of 2026-07-29 was "both
203	halves of the pointwise presentation are witness-free, and what remains is a `cechPicClass`
204	base-change identity at every extension of `κ(t)`, strictly more than `IsChartDatumPlusFibre`
205	asks".  That gap is now closed in the *cheap* direction the row did not expect: the extra
206	strength is not extra content, because the identity at `L` is the identity at `κ(t)` pushed
207	along `PicEtAff.map`.  `isChartDatumPlusFibreAt_self` measured the gap from below (at
208	`L := κ(t)` the two coincide by `Iff.rfl`); this measures it from above, and the two together say
209	the generalisation in `L` costs nothing.
210

98	noncomputable def divRepPullAt
99	    (U : ∀ (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J),
100	      DivFamZar C (ChartRing i j) pi g)
101	    {S : Type u} [CommRing S] [Algebra k S]
102	    (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J)
103	    (omega : ChartRing i j →ₐ[k] S) : DivFamZar C S pi g :=
104	  DivFamZar.mapAlgHom omega (U i j)
105	
106	set_option linter.unusedSectionVars false in
107	@[simp]
108	theorem divRepPullAt_id
109	    (U : ∀ (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J),
110	      DivFamZar C (ChartRing i j) pi g)
111	    (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J) :
112	    divRepPullAt (hpi := hpi) g r1 r2 b1 b2 U i j (AlgHom.id k (ChartRing i j))
113	      = U i j :=
114	  DivFamZar.mapAlgHom_id _
115	
116	set_option linter.unusedSectionVars false in
117	/-- Pulling a chart class through two algebra maps is the same as pulling it through
118	their composite.  This is the algebraic part of F5 naturality. -/
119	theorem divRepPullAt_comp
120	    (U : ∀ (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J),
121	      DivFamZar C (ChartRing i j) pi g)
122	    {S T : Type u} [CommRing S] [Algebra k S] [CommRing T] [Algebra k T]
123	    (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J)
124	    (omega : ChartRing i j →ₐ[k] S) (phi : S →ₐ[k] T) :
125	    DivFamZar.mapAlgHom phi (divRepPullAt (hpi := hpi) g r1 r2 b1 b2 U i j omega)
126	      = divRepPullAt (hpi := hpi) g r1 r2 b1 b2 U i j (phi.comp omega) :=
127	  (DivFamZar.mapAlgHom_comp omega phi (U i j)).symm

129	namespace DivRepChartFamily
130	
131	/-- The precise F5 overlap obligation for a supplied family of classes on every carve
132	chart: two chart points inducing the same morphism to `DivScheme` have equal pulled
133	locally certified divisor classes.  The future universal-family construction proves this
134	from its epsilon identity and the total mono theorem. -/
135	def IsCompatible
136	    (U : ∀ (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J),
137	      DivFamZar C (ChartRing i j) pi g) : Prop :=
138	  ∀ {S : Type u} [CommRing S] [Algebra k S]
139	    (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J)
140	    (i' : (glueData k g r1).J) (j' : (glueData k g r2).J)
141	    (omega : ChartRing i j →ₐ[k] S) (omega' : ChartRing i' j' →ₐ[k] S),
142	    Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom omega.toRingHom) ≫ ChartMap i j
143	        = Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom omega'.toRingHom) ≫ ChartMap i' j' →
144	      divRepPullAt (hpi := hpi) g r1 r2 b1 b2 U i j omega
145	        = divRepPullAt (hpi := hpi) g r1 r2 b1 b2 U i' j' omega'

148	/-- Compatibility may be applied when both chart presentations are identified with a
149	common morphism.  This is the form used on overlaps of an atlas factorization. -/
150	theorem pullAt_eq_of_eq_common
151	    (U : ∀ (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J),
152	      DivFamZar C (ChartRing i j) pi g)
153	    (hU : IsCompatible (hpi := hpi) g r1 r2 b1 b2 U)
154	    {S : Type u} [CommRing S] [Algebra k S]
155	    (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J)
156	    (i' : (glueData k g r1).J) (j' : (glueData k g r2).J)
157	    (omega : ChartRing i j →ₐ[k] S) (omega' : ChartRing i' j' →ₐ[k] S)
158	    (q : Spec (CommRingCat.of S) ⟶
159	      DivScheme k (windowS_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi)
160	        (windowM_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi) g r1 r2 b1
161	        (b2.map (windowShiftEquiv hpi g).symm))
162	    (homega : Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom omega.toRingHom) ≫ ChartMap i j = q)
163	    (homega' : Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom omega'.toRingHom) ≫ ChartMap i' j' = q) :
164	    divRepPullAt (hpi := hpi) g r1 r2 b1 b2 U i j omega
165	      = divRepPullAt (hpi := hpi) g r1 r2 b1 b2 U i' j' omega' :=
166	  hU i j i' j' omega omega' (homega.trans homega'.symm)

168	end DivRepChartFamily

170	/-! ## F6: package a completed affine pullback as an equivalence -/
171	
172	/-- The exact output expected from F5 before the affine equivalence is packaged.
173	`isDivRepClassify_pull` is the hom-side law in the refinement-stable clause spelling;
174	classifier uniqueness turns it into the second inverse law automatically. -/
175	structure DivRepAffinePullback where
176	  pull : ∀ (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S],
177	    (overSpec k S ⟶ DivOver) → DivFamZar C S pi g
178	  pull_classify : ∀ (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S]
179	    (F : DivFamZar C S pi g),
180	    pull S (divRepClassifyZar hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 S F) = F
181	  isDivRepClassify_pull : ∀ (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S]
182	    (v : overSpec k S ⟶ DivOver),
183	    IsDivRepClassify hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 (pull S v) v.left
184	  pull_naturality : ∀ {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
185	    [CommRing B] [Algebra k B] (phi : A →ₐ[k] B) (v : overSpec k A ⟶ DivOver),
186	    pull B (Over.overSpecMap phi ≫ v) = DivFamZar.mapAlgHom phi (pull A v)
187	
188	namespace DivRepAffinePullback
189	
190	/-- The affine representability equivalence assembled from an F5 pullback package.
191	The inverse is the landed backward classifier; its hom-side inverse law follows from
192	`divRepClassifyZar_eq_of_isDivRepClassify`. -/
193	noncomputable def equiv
194	    (D : DivRepAffinePullback hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2)
195	    (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S] :
196	    (overSpec k S ⟶ DivOver) ≃ DivFamZar C S pi g where
197	  toFun := D.pull S
198	  invFun := divRepClassifyZar hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 S
199	  left_inv v :=
200	    (divRepClassifyZar_eq_of_isDivRepClassify hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2
201	      (D.pull S v) v (D.isDivRepClassify_pull S v)).symm
202	  right_inv := D.pull_classify S
203	
204	@[simp]
205	theorem equiv_apply
206	    (D : DivRepAffinePullback hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2)
207	    (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S] (v : overSpec k S ⟶ DivOver) :
208	    equiv (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (hO := hO) (hchi := hchi) (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2)
209	        (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) D S v = D.pull S v :=
210	  rfl

214	    (D : DivRepAffinePullback hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2)
215	    (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S] (F : DivFamZar C S pi g) :
216	    (equiv (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (hO := hO) (hchi := hchi) (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2)
217	      (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) D S).symm F
218	      = divRepClassifyZar hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 S F :=
219	  rfl

221	/-- Naturality of the assembled affine equivalence, in the frozen DDR-9 spelling. -/
222	theorem equiv_naturality
223	    (D : DivRepAffinePullback hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2)
224	    {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
225	    [CommRing B] [Algebra k B] (phi : A →ₐ[k] B)
226	    (v : overSpec k A ⟶ DivOver) :
227	    equiv (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (hO := hO) (hchi := hchi) (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2)
228	        (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) D B (Over.overSpecMap phi ≫ v)
